records.procedure: At your original regular-turn end, bank at most one genuinely unused NORMAL allowance: your wholly unspent movement budget, ordinary free object interaction, or unused ordinary Bonus Action. You must be conscious, able to act and actually possess it; prohibited, extra, borrowed, banked, readied or generated allowances cannot fund a token. Movement requires zero movement spent this turn; snapshot actual legal distance and modes. Consume the chosen allowance into one typed token; hold at most two, expiring at encounter end. On a later own regular turn, spend at most one token of each type without Action for its exact purpose: move up to min(stored feet, current legal normal Speed), one ordinary interaction, or one currently legal BA ability. Pay current terrain; modes must still exist. No conversion to full Action, Reaction, work time or new token, and no refresh of feature uses/cadences. After the second token spent in the real encounter, record one irrevocable fatigue cost due at encounter end: NEW one Core Exhaustion level, with actual immunity/recovery and lethal level 6 rules. Further spending creates no extra fatigue under this source but cannot erase the cost. No Time Loop, rewind or resource restoration.

records.payloadOperational: After your personally cast noncopy spell deals positive resolved damage, optionally apply one Agony record to one living damaged target, once per owner/target/numbered round. Reapplication refreshes one profile without stacked dice. It deals 1d4 necrotic at the next three original target regular-start markers; a CON save against the generating cast DC at each affected regular end, including a current turn if applicable, ends it. The final third scheduled pulse ends the record after damage; no extra ending save afterward. It is a magical ongoing wound, not Core Wound, maximum HP injury or Bleeding by name. NEW a legal positive-potential magical heal or Action Medicine vs source DC ends it; suppressed records remain curable. While active, disadvantage applies only to actual existing CON saves to regain HP and actual saves against resurrection effects; no such save is invented. Death suspends living damage, retaining only the unexpired record tied to that exact death instance until the original third-start deadline; missed pulses are consumed, never backlogged. A legal revival closes that corpse-specific resurrection rider and retains only any still-future living pulse schedule until cured/expired. This grants no resurrection block or permission. Secondary ticks cannot create further Agony, copies, lifesteal or resource procs. Any independent Necrotic Affinity seal needs its own real fatal-root predicate.

copyProfileContract.status: NEW proposed finite feat-copy interface; the five actual Mirrorsage cards/engine are comparisons, not automatic grants.
copyProfileContract.capture: Capture only one directly witnessed resolved component that actually expresses one profile below. Record canonical source/event, actual original spell rank or pre-encounter monster effective rank, native magnitude before external bonuses/defenses, selected type/profile and qualifying own casting route. For monster abilities without a spell rank, use max(1, min(9, ceil(actualCR/2))); missing CR needs a rating assigned before the encounter, never a favorable after-the-fact guess. No unique/legendary/boss feature without an independently reviewed exception; no copying copies, class engines, actions, resources, permanent changes, resurrection, creation, items or protected information. An unsupported role is ineligible, not a blank Director permission.
copyProfileContract.rankAndPayment: For original rank 0, q=0; otherwise q=max(1, floor(originalRank/2)). The chosen actual owned spellcasting route must independently support learning q; merely owning a pool or feat prerequisite does not. Use that route’s real ability for attack/DC and spell components V/S, normal rank price 0/2/3/5/7/10/13/17/21/26 plus actual adjustments. It grants a temporary feat-copy route only, never the original full spell. Spellcasting time is oneAction. At release pay/cast/history/interrupt once, with copy-provenance flags disabling copy/resource/class-proc chains. An explicit source such as Mirrorsage retains its own actual profile/rank/payment instead of being silently converted. FINAL FS-08: these releases are paid feat-copy casts with actual RP/components/history, not ordinary knowledge grants. Boon uses one feat-copy-boon family; its repeated copies do not add, while genuinely distinct eligible ordinary feat bonuses use FS-03.
copyProfileContract.numericBound: For numeric damage/heal/ward select one witnessed native component/type and record its rolled or fixed magnitude B before external bonuses, saves, defenses and recipient caps. If that magnitude was hidden, the Director records it privately; no free identification is given. At feat-copy release roll (q+1)d6, then bound the native numeric result to min(roll, floor(B/2)). No copied critical multiplier, external damage/heal modifier, converted excess or extra recipients. Actual recipient defenses and healing limits still apply. A zero ceiling cannot produce a numeric benefit. This is an explicit NEW meaning of half potency, not an assertion about original undefined wording.
copyProfileContract.lifecycle: At most one feat-copy release per owner per numbered round across Eldritch Echo, Mimicry and adapted copies. A Mirrorsage owner also spends its existing shared release allowance; an unowned Mirrorsage engine is not granted. Strike/Burst/Mend are immediate. Ward/Hindrance/Boon/Step use their stated maximum two-interval duration; source-specific shorter hold deadlines still govern. Only one pending feat-copy record across Eldritch Echo/Mimicry; before a new capture choose whether to replace the old, losing its paid capture/use without refund. Adaptation may retain permission but creates no second release allowance. No copied effect grants extra Action/BA/Reaction, persistent body, loot, learning or concentration capacity.

eldritchBlast.castingAbility: CHA; both feat grants share this one source ability/identity, not two selectable histories.
eldritchBlast.effect: Make one spell attack for 1d10 force. Explicit total-character-level scaling supplies 2 beams at 5,3 at 11,4 at 17; declare each target before its attack, each must be perceived within 60 ft/line of effect. Different legal recipients allowed; each beam is a separate hit/damage event. Ordinary critical doubles that beam’s die only. No CHA damage modifier, pushing or automatic extra effect. floraBody.status: NEW finite conjured body for the feat; no origin/spirit ontology decided.
floraBody.size: Tiny, occupies a supported 5 ft square as a low plant; does not block traversal or grant cover; zeroSpeed and no voluntary movement. Can be carried only as an ordinary object-body interaction; lifting/uprooting ends it immediately without harvest.
floraBody.statistics: Plant creature; no assumed language, mind immunity or world-origin claim. AC 12, HP 5+owner PB snapshotted at creation; saves +owner PB, other checks +0. No damage/condition immunities or special senses unless an actual source grants them. It perceives commands within 60 ft through ordinary sight/hearing; Silence matters for spoken commands. It has no independent initiative, Action, Bonus Action or Reaction, and no attack outside the commanded profiles or the final expressly bounded Trapcasting exception. Zero HP permanently destroys it instead of creating a dying body. No corpse, reward, harvest, resource/soul collection, loot or Supply credit. Ordinary legal damage and healing may affect the actual creature but cannot recreate a destroyed plant, refill its creation entitlement or extend its deadline.
floraBody.dc: At acquisition select one actual possessed spellcasting route; use DC 8+current PB+that route’s current ability modifier. No phantom Wisdom/Spellcraft statistic. Actual source-specific component/target defenses still apply.
floraBody.cadence: Action creates;1/SR or LR, capacity 1 or 2 at 10. This one extra creation entitlement is bound to that original committed use and is consumed once; if missed/lost it is not banked. Each plant has its own original minute deadline. No replacement/revival can restore the entitlement. Any command, trap orBurst with a hostile result uses the owner’s one shared offensive-companion allowance per numbered round; one selected mode outcome for the coordinated group. Ordinary command: owner shared Bonus Action, actual perceptible60ft channel, attached phase after owner regular turn. One action outcome and one offensive allowance per owner/numbered round; Trapcasting spends that same allowance at its exact entry/burst event. No independent turn is added.

Its selected creation mode additionally determines its Spore or Entangle option and its Trapcasting result/burst type; selecting Lash leaves that basic profile. Other plants extend the legal Lash origin as printed but never multiply damage, control areas or offense allowances.

originalFullCatalogRecord.name: Counterspell

operational.activation: Reaction — when another creature you can perceive within range and line of effect begins casting a spell, after its casting costs and cadence are committed but before its effect resolves
operational.targets: One pending spell cast by the triggering creature. The spell needs an actual recorded rank; the Director may know that rank without revealing it to you.
operational.resolution: make a spellcasting-ability check using the actual ability for the class through which you cast Counterspell, adding PB once, against DC 10 + twice the triggering spell's actual rank (rank 0 contributes 0). Use CORE_RESOLUTION_PLAYTEST.md's fixed-DC task degrees and natural shifts: at least DC+10 Critical Success, at least DC Success, at most DC-10 Critical Failure, otherwise Failure; natural 20 improves one degree and natural 1 worsens one. Collapse both upper degrees to success and both lower degrees to failure; invent no additional critical effect. This is not a spell attack or saving throw.
operational.effect: Success negates the selected pending spell after its costs were committed; failure lets it continue. Every interruptible cast first commits its RP/material/other costs, components, concentration transition, Dissonance/Refrain and exact beginning/casting hooks once, then opens the interruption window. A surviving cast later resolves its effect and outcome-dependent hooks. Negation gives no refund, no successful-effect trigger and no restoration of old concentration. Counterspell is itself a spell and can be countered. Resolve nested counters last-in, first-out; if a counter is negated, the earlier pending spell resumes without paying or casting again. Resuming a parent never rewrites the later nested cast's Refrain/Dissonance history.
operational.scaling: None. No automatic success against lower ranks and no generic upcast.
operational.limitations: One attempt per creature against a particular pending cast, shared across ordinary, Wizard, Mage and other same-named Counterspell sources. An exact source that expressly grants an additional Counterspell attempt against the same pending cast overrides this default; merely granting another Reaction does not. After a failed attempt another eligible creature may react; once negated, the spell supplies no further interruption trigger. All reactions need their own legal remaining resource, components, range and current source permissions. Attempting does not reveal spell identity/rank; never treat an unassigned rank as 0 or estimate it from RP. Ready opens its cast-interruption window at preparation, not release. Countering is not whole-Action/turn hard denial and does not spend that ledger. Ordinary Counterspell requires ordinary repertoire/class access and rank-3 cost; Wizard/Mage same-named class cards keep their own separate acquisition, printed costs, ranks, recharge and text. Apply SPELL_INTEGRATION_RULES.md for actual class access and repertoire, costs before resolution, components, concentration, Dissonance/Refrain and exact source cadence. No automatic scaling or generic upcast.
operational.designNotes: PRESERVED: both Abjuration/Universal rank-3 placements, Reaction, 60 feet, V/S/F and instantaneous interruption. NEW: actual casting ability+PB against DC 10+2*rank, one attempt per pending cast, hidden-rank handling and nested timing. REVIEWED SOURCE CORRECTION: the earlier binary-check proposal is superseded by the existing Core fixed-DC task rule, with natural shifts and collapsed success/failure outcomes. Exact source permission may override the shared attempt limit; another Reaction alone cannot.
operational.implementationStatus: REVIEWED authored operational-playtest manuscript; runtime and balance validation pending

operational.targets: One individually perceptible ongoing magical effect within range and line of effect, generated by a spell of actual recorded rank 0 through 3.
operational.resolution: Automatic for an eligible effect; no saving throw or check.

originalFullCatalogRecord.name: Slow

operational.targets: Actual Enchantment mode: choose up to six creatures you perceive within 60 feet and line of effect. Actual Transmutation mode: the triggering creature must be perceived within 60 feet and line of effect and must be selected; choose up to five additional such creatures. The actual casting class determines school/mode; paying the same rank-3/base-5-RP price never grants the other package.
operational.duration: Both modes: concentration, up to one minute. In initiative, the maximum ends at the caster's tenth future regular-turn START after application, excluding any start already underway/passed. If begun outside initiative, the maximum is 60 elapsed seconds. Preserve the original virtual marker/absolute deadline through initiative changes, extra turns, absence and planar travel; no timing-mode change resets it.
operational.resolution: Enchantment uses an Action and an independent Wisdom save per target. Transmutation uses a Reaction when a creature you perceive within 60 feet/line of effect begins a distinct voluntary movement segment or begins an Action on its own actual turn, after required declaration/commitment and before the segment’s first step or Action’s first main outcome. An extra turn can trigger; Bonus Actions and Reactions cannot. Transmutation gives each chosen target an independent Constitution save. Success: no new effect for that target. Failure: apply only that actual mode’s independently defended rider set. Each affected creature repeats that mode’s recorded WIS or CON save at every affected regular-turn END, including the current regular turn if applied during it; success ends that cast’s application on that creature. Extra turns grant no ending saves. Outside initiative an otherwise legally established ongoing effect uses the specifically bound six-second END-save cadence, never a new Reaction trigger.
operational.effect: Enchantment failure: half Speed under existing strongest-adverse-Speed arbitration; -2 AC; -2 Dexterity ability checks and Dexterity saving throws, expressly excluding initiative; and at most one full Action commitment per actual turn. It changes no DEX score/modifier, DEX attack/damage, spell DC or other unnamed derived statistic. AC has only its separate -2. Count an Action already committed before application toward the ceiling; an already-legally-committed second Action still finishes, but no further Action can be committed that turn. The ceiling applies independently on extra turns; it retains Bonus Actions, Reactions and inherent attacks in a legal Attack Action. Transmutation failure: half Speed, -2 AC and no future Reaction commitments. It imposes no DEX penalty or Action ceiling. Already-committed unresolved Reactions remain on the LIFO stack. Neither mode grants unprinted spell delay, attack-count restriction, Action/Bonus-Action interchange, cancellation or teleport restriction.
operational.scaling: None. No automatic increase in range, targets, duration, magnitude or uses.
operational.limitations: Transmutation’s movement trigger is one distinct segment, such as moving, performing an Action, then resuming movement; choosing another square during continuous movement is not a new segment, and individual feet/tiles are never new triggers. A paid Slow remains independent if a legal nested interruption removes the original parent Action: resolve it against still-legal selected targets, without refund, revival or parent cancellation. A surviving parent Action continues after the interrupt stack; movement recalculates remaining legal allowance before the next expenditure, keeping all movement already spent. The one-Action ceiling, Reaction denial and other soft riders do not claim whole-Action hard-control allowance. Actual narrowly scoped defenses can suppress individual components. Each cast/mode retains separate caster, concentration, saves and deadline. Half-Speed records compete against the same pre-control Speed, then existing later systemic multipliers apply. Identical Slow -2 AC and DEX penalties do not add; independent Enchantment and Transmutation casts may supply their distinct surviving riders together. Enchantment access: Bard, Crimson Agent, Mirrorsage, Thief, Wizard, Paladin. Transmutation access: Dragoon, Druid, Mage, Monk, Ranger, Shaman, Tinker. Preserve each exact minimum class level. The accompanying ENCHANTMENT_RANK3_INTEGRATION_PLAYTEST.md supplies the expressly bound timing/component procedure; it grants no extra turn, action, hidden information or source access. Actual class access/repertoire, legal action/components/RP, concentration transitions, Dissonance/Refrain and paid cast/counter order follow SPELL_INTEGRATION_RULES.md. A legal cast pays before hidden eligibility/effect resolution; failure or countering refunds nothing and restores no displaced concentration. V is audible, S needs the ordinary usable hand, and F is the normal class focus. Saves use the actual casting class's spell DC and binary-save rules. Hidden eligibility supplies no free diagnostic. Creature type alone supplies no mental immunity; Charmed-only immunity has only its actual condition scope. No generic upcast, extra action budget or resource generation.
operational.designNotes: PRESERVED: both school/rank-3 modes, 60 feet, V/S/F, up to six targets; Enchantment Action/half Speed/-2 AC/-2 DEX/one action, and Transmutation Reaction/half Speed/-2 AC/no Reactions. NEW: WIS versus CON, concentration minute/repeat END saves, explicit distinct-segment/Action Reaction window with mandatory triggering target, scoped DEX exception and full-Action ceiling. No mode union from a single cast; independent overlaps keep provenance.

originalFullCatalogRecord.name: Future Echo

operational.targets: Yourself and/or any willing allies you perceive within 60 feet and line of effect at resolution, each with an actual regular encounter initiative slot.
operational.duration: Pending until the next numbered round boundary, then one affected round of initiative permutation; no concentration.
operational.resolution: No save. While an encounter initiative order exists, choose the eligible participants and record their desired relative order at resolution. Range, perception, willingness and allied status are checked then, with no later range tether. Outside initiative a legal cast has no scheduling effect and refunds no committed cost. This spell does not create initiative to manufacture a round. One pending Future Echo per caster; a later successful cast before execution replaces that caster’s pending schedule.
operational.effect: After the current round’s final slot and normal end-round events finish, and before the next round’s first regular start, restore any prior round’s Future Echo permutation to the baseline, retaining changes made by other exact initiative rules. Then resolve pending Future Echo schedules in application order, with stable source/mechanical order breaking genuinely simultaneous ties. For each schedule, remove selected participants who no longer possess regular encounter slots and those already claimed by an earlier Future Echo at this boundary. Gather only the remaining participants’ own baseline slot positions, sort those positions earliest to latest, and assign those participants to them in the recorded relative order. Every remaining participant is claimed by that application even if a one-person set leaves its position unchanged. Enemy, unselected and skipped participants’ slots do not move. Removed participants’ abandoned baseline slots are not redistributed. Late entrants not selected at cast resolution are not added automatically. An Incapacitated participant retaining a regular slot remains in the permutation and obeys its actual restrictions.
operational.scaling: None. No automatic increase in range, duration, targets, uses or information.
operational.limitations: Each affected participant receives exactly one ordinary regular turn in the affected numbered round, with its normal movement, Action/Bonus Action permissions and regular-start Reaction refresh/recharge/death-save processing as applicable. The permutation itself creates no turn, Action, Reaction, recharge, save, pulse, fall step or recovery. Existing effects retain their previously recorded virtual markers, absolute deadlines and actual periodic clocks; a moved regular turn must not replay an already-scheduled fixed event. Effects newly created during the affected round use the actual schedule then in force. At the following boundary, the prior baseline resumes unless another exact initiative rule changes it; no midround restoration creates a duplicate or missing turn. Pending schedules can be countered, dispelled or suppressed only under an actual applicable rule. A pending schedule unavailable at its execution boundary expires without a delayed makeup. Boundary execution consumes the pending magic and records a fixed one-round turn assignment; later dispelling/suppressing that completed cast does not reverse an already-committed schedule midround. A fresh cast during the affected round can prepare the following round, after baseline restoration. Caster death alone does not erase an independent pending schedule, but a selected caster who loses their actual slot is filtered normally. Source-specific companion turns qualify only if they genuinely own regular slots, not merely for acting after an owner. Full Time Loop and its unimplemented runtime are not enabled by this manuscript. Actual class access, repertoire, V/S/F components, costs, Dissonance/Refrain, beginning hooks, concentration transitions and interruption follow SPELL_INTEGRATION_RULES.md. Commit costs before the counter window; failed, blocked and countered effects do not refund costs or restore prior concentration. Use the actual casting class's school and rank. Specific information protections apply to their actual subjects and generating-source scope. Hidden unprotected facts are readable; undefined facts are not invented. No automatic scaling or generic upcast.
operational.designNotes: PRESERVED: Action/60 feet/V,S,F and choosing ally initiative order next round. NEW: willing selected set, permutation among existing slots for one round, no concentration, baseline restoration and first-application claims. Exact completions specify baseline-before-next-permutation ordering, singleton claims, suppression at the execution boundary and an atomic schedule commitment that cannot be dispelled into a broken midround order.

engine: Intelligence is the class ability; use d8 Hit Die from the detailed book, recording the older runtime d6 as superseded for this draft. You begin with 3 empty Echo Slots. Expansion II raises ordinary capacity 5; Sacred/Floating memory features may add one restricted slot, but total concurrent stored Echoes never exceeds 6. Slots are storage, not spell slots. Releasing normally empties that record. Rest restores RP, not spent Echoes. Starting a new encounter does not duplicate the archive.

Mirrorbind is an Action, once per encounter, against a creature within 60 ft whose eligible ability you saw resolve since the start of your previous turn. Target must have INT 6 or lower, not be a boss or possess unique/legendary status unless an encounter script explicitly permits copying. It makes WIS save versus class DC; failure captures one witnessed ability into an empty slot. No copying from allies, your companions, another copy, a corpse, a recharge-limited legendary power or an at-will source that itself restores resources. You can voluntarily erase a slot without an action on your turn, permanently losing its record.

Record source creature/name, witnessed ability, category, damage type, allowed rank, capture encounter and whether first release has occurred. For this pilot, capture copies the observed role into ONE bounded profile: Strike=one target 60 ft class spell attack S d8 observed damage type; Burst=up to 3 enemies in 10 ft radius within 30 ft DEX save S d6, half on success; Mend=one living ally 30 ft S d6+M HP; Ward=one ally 30 ft S d6+M temporary HP for 1 minute; Hindrance=one enemy 30 ft WIS save or Speed-10 ft and no Reactions until end its next turn. Choose only a profile actually expressed by the observed source; physical attack cannot become healing. Rank is max(1, ceil(source challenge rating/2)); if source lacks a rating the Director assigns a rank before the encounter, not after seeing a desirable ability. Rank cannot exceed your Mirrorsage learnable rank; no copying character levels from a creature. Damage/targets/control are capped by these profiles, not source boss dice.

Echo Release costs the Core V 2 RP cost of the recorded rank, minimum 2, consumes its record and counts as a spell for Dissonance and Refrain. Spell attack/DC use your own stats. First release of a newly captured record ignores Refrain addition only; base strain remains. Any preserved subsequent release uses ordinary repeated-spell strain. All released Echoes, pet replays, fusions and reflections share ONE release action per round; a specifically combined package counts once but pays for every component and has its printed damage cap. Copies cannot create resources or recursive Echoes.

One Mirror Beast OR Reflective Companion, never both. Mirror Beast uses standard companion stats, initially copies appearance only, and costs a Bonus Action to command. You may command it to make its normal attack OR originate your round's Echo Release from its position, paying RP and consuming the record normally; not both. You still supply an Action for release unless a feature specifically changes that action cost. A shifted appearance grants no extra actions/stats. Destroying/dismissing it grants no capture, corpse, XP or recovery. Charm Bind is 1/long rest, 3 rounds, concentration, INT 6-or-lower target WIS save and repeat at each turn end/when harmed by your side; never a player character or boss without explicit encounter permission. A charmed companion uses its own ordinary attack with damage capped at standard companion S d6; unique spells/powers remain unavailable.

Focus Point is a separate resource: when Mimicry Focus is known, receive 1 at encounter start, maximum 1, lost at encounter end. It can modify one Echo without generating another release, recapture or resource refund. No stacking damage doublings; use the printed modest die/range boost. Healing/support copies always consume RP and cannot restore RP or duplicate limited-use features.

Standard acquisition applies; baseline Mirrorbind, Echo Release and summon procedure become usable by selecting their cards. Echo Channeling and Mirrorcall are upgrades, not duplicate mandatory unlocks. The contradiction between source initial 3 slots and Expansion I 2→3 is reconciled as an archive-safety upgrade below. currentGoverningExcerpts.heading: Which rule applies
currentGoverningExcerpts.exactText:
## Which rule applies

The domain authority is [Core Systems Known Descent V2](../../../../books/player/Decennium_Descent_Core_Systems_Bible_v2_Known_Descent.docx). The approved [Player Rulebook V6](../../../../books/player/Decennium_Descent_Player_Rulebook_v6.docx) supplies compatible rules that Core does not replace. This overlay states the selected interpretation or newly authored rule wherever those sources leave a gap. An explicit exception on an operative, reviewed class/spell/item card applies only within its printed scope; a historical alternate or a same-named feature is not an extra grant. This candidate does not promote an entire historical branch.

| Question | Active rule and provenance | Inactive alternate |
|---|---|---|
| Attacks | Core V2: meet AC; natural 1 misses; natural 20 hits and doubles damage dice. | Applying the general Gameplay four-degree roll to attacks. |
| Task checks | Explicitly adopted Gameplay four degrees and natural shifts. | Assuming every critical result creates an unprinted effect. |
| Ordinary saves | Binary meet-DC test; printed failure margins remain literal. Natural 1/20 do not generically shift saves in this candidate. This separation is an integration choice. | Automatic critical saves or natural-result shifts inferred from the task rule. |
| Death-save timing | Core and V6: start of turn; regular-turn-only timing is a provisional guard. | Gameplay end-of-turn saves. |
| Wounds | Core trigger/save, Constitution-save and Hit-Dice-recovery penalties, and three-Wound Critical state. | Gameplay automatic Wound triggers, Hit Dice healing penalty, half Speed and Strain lock. |
| Named Wounded condition | Core paragraph 782 expressly describes the same Wound count, Constitution penalty, Hit Dice recovery and three-Wound Critical state. Apply those records once. | V6 Appendix A paragraphs 9971–9974 give a conflicting temporary condition cleared by magic/rest with Constitution-save disadvantage; Core replaces it here. |
| Stable, instant death, knockout and temporary HP | Compatible recovered V6 rules. | Treating these recovered rules as newly invented. |
| Ordinary Wound treatment | Explicit Gameplay-derived integration below. | Claiming it is original Core wording or ordinary HP healing. |
| Injury table and unresolved thresholds | New provisional choices below, with their search limits stated. | Dropping Core's failure-by-5 consequence because its table was not located. |

currentGoverningExcerpts.heading: Rolls
currentGoverningExcerpts.exactText:
## Rolls

Choose the roll type before rolling. Use the actual ability modifier, including negative values, and normal proficiency only when applicable. Existing advantage/disadvantage chooses the higher/lower of two d20s; multiple sources do not stack, and any advantage plus disadvantage cancels. Add other legal modifiers once. Fractions round down unless a rule specifies otherwise. One tile is 5 feet. Class L, S and effect M retain their definitions in the shared class rules.

**Attack:** roll d20 plus the appropriate attack modifier against AC. Meeting AC hits. Natural 1 always misses; natural 20 always hits and critically doubles damage dice, not flat modifiers. Beating AC by 10 is not a critical hit. An explicit broader critical range does not stack with another; use the broadest eligible range. In this overlay, a natural result below 20 in that range must still meet AC unless the feature expressly says it always hits.

**Task, skill or tool check against a fixed DC:** total at least DC+10 is Critical Success; at least DC is Success; at most DC-10 is Critical Failure; other totals below DC are Failure. Natural 20 then improves one degree and natural 1 worsens one, bounded at either end. A task printing only success/failure collapses the two upper degrees to success and two lower degrees to failure; no extra consequence is invented. A natural 20 can still fail an otherwise impossible check, and a natural 1 with sufficient modifiers can still succeed.

**Saving throw:** total at least DC succeeds; otherwise it fails. Natural 1 and 20 have no generic special outcome. A printed failure by 5 or 10 compares the final total with the DC; it does not add an unprinted critical-save system. Death saves are the specific exception below.

**Opposed check, new provisional tie rule:** compare final totals. Higher wins; an exact tie leaves the existing state unchanged, so the initiating creature fails to change it. Do not turn task natural shifts into hidden numeric modifiers. A maneuver explicitly printing degree outcomes must specify how those apply.

currentGoverningExcerpts.heading: Resolve a damage event
currentGoverningExcerpts.exactText:
## Resolve a damage event

Resolve each genuinely separate hit or damage event once. Do not split one packet to multiply Wound saves or combine separate hits merely to cross a threshold. Feature-specific prevention that acts before damage or before reaching zero resolves at its printed timing first.

1. Resolve attack/save, damage and applicable defenses. The remaining nonnegative amount is **resolved damage**.
2. Record HP, Wounds and zero-HP state before the event. Remove temporary HP first. **Post-temp damage = resolved damage minus temporary HP absorbed.** Keep this amount even when it exceeds current HP; floor the resulting current HP at zero.
3. Check V6 Instant Death. If post-temp damage minus HP before the hit is at least maximum HP, the creature dies. For a creature already at zero, this is post-temp damage at least maximum HP. Stop: there is no Wound save, death-save failure or successful knockout from that event.
4. Otherwise, a living creature makes one Wound save if it dropped from positive HP to zero, if **2 × post-temp damage is at least maximum HP**, or if the effect actually inflicts Maiming. Overlapping triggers still cause only one save. The post-temp threshold and one-save rule are new provisional interpretations. Maiming is an independent trigger even when temporary HP absorbs all ordinary damage; immunity to Maiming itself still applies.
5. Make a Constitution save against **max(10, floor(post-temp damage / 2))**. Use pre-event Wounds for the -1-per-Wound penalty. Maiming with zero post-temp damage uses DC 10. A Wound gained now cannot penalize the roll that created it.
6. A success adds no Wound. A failure that began with zero, one or two Wounds adds exactly one; failure by 5 or more also gives that Wound one Injury. A failure that began with three Wounds kills the creature instead: no fourth Wound and no Injury roll. Stop processing later living-target consequences if dead.
7. If the creature was already at zero before this event and post-temp damage is positive, end Stable. A creature using death saves adds one failure, or two for a critical hit; three failures kill it. An ordinary creature that does not use death saves dies instead, without starting death counters. A hit from positive HP to zero does not also cause a same-packet death failure.
8. If this event newly reduces positive HP to zero, a valid melee knockout makes the surviving creature Stable. Otherwise a character/significant NPC using death saves begins dying; an ordinary monster dies. A previously Stable creature whose temporary HP absorbed all damage remains Stable unless an independent Maiming result killed it. The Director identifies significant NPCs consistently. Knockout cannot override Instant Death or a fatal Wound save.

Core's Maiming and Wound trigger rules remain subject to an actual feature's eligibility. The reference helper receives already legal events; it does not grant every attack Maiming or a damage-prevention exception.

currentGoverningExcerpts.heading: Zero HP and recovery
currentGoverningExcerpts.exactText:
## Zero HP and recovery

A living character at zero HP is Unconscious. Core's condition already includes Incapacitated, unawareness, dropping held items and falling Prone; an adjacent hit is critical as specified there. Healing does not silently remove other independent causes of Unconscious or Prone.

While dying, make one death save at the **start of each regular initiative turn**. Roll d20 without modifiers unless a feature specifically modifies death saves. Natural 20 restores 1 HP; natural 1 adds two failures. Other results of 10 or more add one success; 9 or less add one failure. Three successes make the creature Stable; three failures make it Dead. Extra turns and Actions add no extra death saves. Stable or Dead creatures do not roll them.

Regaining positive HP or becoming Stable resets both counters. Temporary HP does not raise normal HP, end Unconscious or reset counters. Fully absorbed damage does not end Stable or add a death failure in this provisional interpretation. Independent Maiming can still cause its Wound save.

**Stabilize:** an Action and DC 10 Wisdom (Medicine) check, or an Action using one healer's-kit use automatically, stabilizes a living dying creature at zero. It remains Unconscious and makes no death saves. Roll 1d4 once when it becomes Stable and record its absolute recovery time that many hours later. If still Stable then, it regains 1 HP. Damage reaching normal HP cancels that deadline and resumes dying with the appropriate failures. Rest and Stable recovery use the same elapsed clock, so four hours of recovery inside an eight-hour Watch do not cost twelve hours. A later rest does not separately replay the Stable healing event.

**Dead:** ordinary healing and stabilization do not restore life. Resurrection must satisfy its own willing-soul, body, time, cost and target rules. It does not automatically remove Wounds, Corruption, debts, legal death or claims upon the body. Corpses cannot supply repeated resource triggers.

currentGoverningExcerpts.heading: Encounter and action resources
currentGoverningExcerpts.exactText:
## Encounter and action resources

Establish terrain, light, hazards, objectives, exits and cargo; determine awareness; roll `d20 + DEX modifier + legal bonuses`. Highest first. Players choose player/player ties; the Director resolves ties involving NPCs. Keep the resulting ordered slots for the encounter. A round represents approximately six seconds. A **regular turn** is a creature's normal initiative slot even if it cannot act. An extra turn is distinct.

A turn normally permits movement, one Action, a Bonus Action when an actual rule grants a use, and one ordinary free object interaction. A second ordinary interaction or an Action-time object activation uses an Action. Brief communication is not an extra Action. Conditions and specific features may restrict these permissions.

The shared limit is one **extra full Action per creature per numbered round**. Such an Action cannot grant another extra Action, Bonus Action or Reaction. This cap is independent of Reaction timing. Extra turns do not by themselves refresh Reactions, recharge, periodic ticks, recovery ticks or the regular-turn allowances defined here.

**Reaction interpretation.** Begin an encounter with one available Reaction unless surprised or otherwise prohibited. Refresh at each regular own-turn start; never at the numbered round boundary or an extra turn. A late-initiative creature can therefore react before its first turn, refresh, and react again in the same numbered round. A legal trigger, available resource and all feature prerequisites are still required.

**Explicit additional Reactions.** A reviewed card can grant a separate limited use without refreshing the ordinary resource. Warrior Mind Shock supplies its stated once-per-duration non-attack Reaction; spending one resource does not consume/reset the other. Surprise, Incapacitated and Focused still restrict both. It grants no Counterspell knowledge or waived costs. Extra turns refresh neither. Per-dose reapplication/stacking and other specific grants remain part of the class semantic pass.

**Surprise — V6 plus NEW Bonus Action clarification.** On a surprised creature's first regular turn it cannot voluntarily move or take an Action or Bonus Action. It cannot react until that turn ends. Its slot, durations, passive effects, concentration, periodic effects and recharge still occur. Surprise alone is not Incapacitated or Unconscious. Brief communication and an otherwise legal simple free interaction remain possible.

**Entry — NEW.** Standard end-round reinforcements roll/receive initiative and first act next round. An explicit midround entrant acts this round only if its complete ordered slot is still upcoming; entry during that exact slot counts as already passed. It has its initial Reaction unless prohibited. A summon-specific timing rule overrides this generic entry procedure.

After the final slot, resolve Core's end-round hazards, reinforcements, morale, objectives and boss phases. Conclude the scene with surrender, capture, pursuit, harvesting access and noise consequences under their own rules; winning initiative does not resolve those automatically.

currentGoverningExcerpts.heading: Time and event ordering — NEW
currentGoverningExcerpts.exactText:
## Time and event ordering — NEW

For a duration created in initiative, record the relevant original regular start/end marker. Existing effects keep that **virtual marker**, repeating every six seconds if the creature leaves or changes initiative. Reordering, rerolling, extra turns, death/removal or leaving/reentering initiative never restart an existing duration. New effects use the current schedule. Source death still ends concentration, a source-dependent aura/tether or an effect explicitly ending on death.

- A bare hostile target-bound **N rounds** ends at the Nth future regular target-end marker. An in-progress target turn's current end does not count.
- A bare self/source buff, ally-targeted buff or source-controlled aura **N rounds** ends at the Nth future source-start marker. Explicit target-turn, pulse or absolute timing overrides this default. Activation during source turn 1 for three rounds ends at source turn 4's start.
- **Next turn** means the next future regular turn of the named creature, not the current turn's still-upcoming end. An unqualified next turn refers to source/user under the existing shared rule. Explicit “this turn” can include the current turn.
- An outside-initiative bare N-round effect instead gets an absolute application-time + N×6 seconds deadline. Entering initiative preserves that deadline.
- Explicit periodic profiles retain their registered clocks and tick counts. Never create a second timer merely because a generic duration rule also exists.

The [exact GPT review](../../../../docs/audit/2026-10-08/full-game/GPT_COMBAT_EXACT_FINDINGS.md) confirms ally-buff source clocks and excluding the current turn for explicit next-turn endpoints. The helper excludes a specific current-end marker only if that marker would otherwise be selected: application during a turn at time1 with end3 excludes3 and selects9; application at/after3 also selects9, without erroneously skipping again to15.

At a regular turn's **start**, resolve in this order:

1. Expire start-ending effects and apply immediate state changes from those expirations.
2. Refresh Reaction; tick regular-start recharge/non-action clocks.
3. Resolve already-due absolute state recovery if now legal, including a previously blocked Stable recovery deadline.
4. If still alive, dying and at 0 HP with death saves, make that turn's death save.
5. Resolve other start effects and periodic events in application order.
6. Begin voluntary turn decisions.

At **end**, resolve triggered effects, due damage, saves and maintenance before end-ending effects expire; then the slot finishes. No extra turn creates another regular marker. The caller must not reuse a resolved marker.

For simultaneous effects, earlier application timestamp precedes later. For simultaneous components of one source, its printed internal order controls; otherwise use stable application sequence, with source/mechanical ID as a final tie-break. Record that sequence when creating the effects. Beneficial/harmful labels do not change priority. Periodic family arbitration happens once per family/marker before its damage, retaining the family registry's consumed loser ticks.

Examples: dying at 0 rolls its death save before ordinary start-turn healing; a fatal death save is not undone by ordinary healing. Stable at 0 skips the save, then start-turn damage can break Stable. A natural 20 can restore 1 HP before a due Bleed drops it to 0 as a new drop event. If Decay expires while a Stable recovery deadline is already due, the old deadline resolves once without rerolling recovery time.

currentGoverningExcerpts.heading: Ready
currentGoverningExcerpts.exactText:
## Ready

Spend an Action to declare a perceivable trigger and one legal Action-time action or movement. It expires next regular own-turn start. **NEW:** only one pending Ready per creature; replacing it loses the prior setup and any paid held-spell costs. No Bonus Action/Reaction ability, long ritual or multi-minute activity can be prepared by generic Ready.

The trigger happens first, then the readied response immediately follows before later events, unless a specific effect explicitly interrupts. On release spend the normal Reaction and recheck target, range, sight/perception, line of effect, ammunition and other prerequisites. An invalid or declined occurrence spends no release resource; the Ready can wait for another valid occurrence before expiry. This does not undo setup costs. Once released, it is consumed.

For ordinary nonspell actions, feature/ammunition costs are paid on release unless text charges setup. A readied **Attack Action** gets its legally available ordinary attack count; a feature limited to your own turn does not thereby work off-turn. Core Overwatch is explicitly one ranged attack, not that full Attack Action and not Soldier's distinct engine.

A readied spell is actually **cast at preparation**: choose spell/mode, verify legality, pay RP/material/other costs, provide components, resolve Dissonance/Refrain and cast-trigger effects once. Counterspell/cast-interruption opportunity occurs then, not again at release. Every held spell requires concentration, even ordinarily non-concentration spells; incompatible prior concentration ends. Lost concentration loses the held spell and costs. NEW: select the legal target/area point at release and recheck legality without repaying. At release the hold continues as ordinary spell concentration if required, otherwise ends after resolution. Expired/replaced/countered held spells do not refund paid costs.

Ready movement grants a separate current-Speed budget on release, pays terrain costs and can provoke ordinary opportunity attacks. It grants no extra Action, Bonus Action or interaction.

Focused stance's Reaction restriction also blocks an ordinary Ready release; Ready does not create a Counterspell exception. Holding a spell does not waive any current Reaction prohibition.

**Spell-effect duration begins at release.** Its normal duration is anchored when the effect manifests, while Ready expiry and held concentration already run from preparation. A source explicitly tying a particular consequence to casting/preparation retains that consequence's stated clock. No casting cost, Refrain, Dissonance or cast trigger occurs a second time merely from release.

currentGoverningExcerpts.heading: Movement and geometry
currentGoverningExcerpts.exactText:
## Movement and geometry

Track **spent movement cost**, not distance, for ordinary turn movement. Mode cap = `(1 + number of legal Dash actions this turn) × current Speed for that mode`; remaining = max(0, cap − spent cost). Switching modes never refunds cost. Recalculate cap on Speed changes, preserving spent cost. Stand from Prone costs floor(half current Speed) and requires nonzero Speed and enough budget. Dropping Prone costs no movement.

For each foot traveled, normal/difficult/severe terrain costs 1/2/3; use strongest terrain only. Add +1 for crawling and +1 for squeezing. Crawl in difficult =3:1; crawl+squeeze in difficult =4:1. A nonhostile occupied space counts as difficult terrain. Enter a hostile creature's space only with ≥two-size difference or an express feature; never willingly end in an occupied space. Squeeze through a space one size smaller, with own attack/DEX-save disadvantage and attacks-against advantage.

Walk10 through difficult spends20; switch to Fly30 leaves10. Stand with Speed30 spends15; switching to Fly30 leaves15. Two legal Dashes at Speed30 give cap90; prior expenditure still counts. Interpose/Press grant5 budget: they cannot enter a difficult 5-ft tile costing10. Their separate budgets never refill ordinary movement. Ready movement uses Speed at release; Withdraw uses half current Speed. All voluntary movement requires nonzero relevant Speed.

Forced movement does not use these ledgers or provoke ordinary opportunity attacks, cannot place creatures in solid matter, and stops at obstacles. Teleport does not traverse intervening terrain or spend Speed unless printed; it requires a legal destination. Speed0 alone does not block forced movement or teleport. Flight with Prone/Speed0/lost support causes Falling unless Hover or an explicit magical support exception applies; use the existing fixed Fall Marker procedure. Reaching support ends Falling.

NEW grid metric: each orthogonal or diagonal neighboring tile is 5 ft; use the same metric for ordinary ranges/areas. No diagonal cut through a corner when both adjacent orthogonal sides are completely blocked. Exact templates, 3D geometry, mounts, chases, jumping, climbing/swimming procedures and currents need further source review.

currentGoverningExcerpts.heading: Cover, sight, Hide and Search
currentGoverningExcerpts.exactText:
## Cover, sight, Hide and Search

Keep **visibility**, **known location**, and **line of effect** separate. Seeing through a barrier does not itself permit attacking through it. Best cover only: half +2 AC/DEX saves; three-quarters +5; total prevents direct targeting through that obstruction. Never add +2 and +5. For areas, evaluate line/cover from the area's origin to each target; total cover there excludes a creature unless the effect explicitly travels around/through the obstruction. The origin point itself must be legally targetable.

Within normal ranged range, no range penalty; beyond normal through long, disadvantage; beyond long, illegal. Ranged attacks also have disadvantage when within5ft of a non-Incapacitated hostile that can see the attacker, even if the attacker cannot see that hostile. All advantage/disadvantage follows the single cancellation rule.

NEW **Hide**: permitted only against observers unable to see you clearly or where a feature permits. Roll DEX Stealth once, record natural die and total. Against each observer's passive DC `10 + WIS Perception modifier including applicable proficiency`, use the Core four-degree task system. Meet DC succeeds before natural1/20 degree adjustment; Success/Critical Success establishes Hidden for that observer. No unsourced passive ±5 adjustment for advantage/disadvantage. Actual Search rolls use their normal modifiers.

Hidden means that observer cannot see you and does not know your location. Clear sight or learning your position ends Hidden for that observer. Moving between hiding places can retain Hidden only if no clear sight/revealing event occurs. A failed Hide cannot simply be rerolled unchanged; a materially new hiding position, concealment, distraction, sight-breaking event or express reroll feature is required. Hidden is not a generic immunity or a free stealth roll for every move.

**Search** Action: WIS Perception for sensory detection; INT Investigation for appropriate traces/deduction; Core Arcana/Engineering where relevant. Directly locating a Hidden creature defaults to Perception against its recorded final Stealth total as a static DC, using task degrees/natural shifts. Success reveals location only to the searcher and ends Hidden for that observer, without automatically granting sight. Communicate normally to inform others. Search can be repeated on later turns by paying the Action.

Attacks against unseen targets have disadvantage; unseen attackers have advantage, subject to the **Core Invisible exception**: once its position is known, Invisible's own attack modifiers end for that observer and cannot immediately return solely because it remains Invisible. Independent darkness, smoke, blindness or hiding can still supply modifiers.

Resolve an attack using pre-attack information; afterward reveal location to observers able to perceive its evidence. If an unseen target's location is unknown, do not directly choose it for a creature-target effect. A weapon/projectile can instead attack a suspected space: wrong space automatically misses; correct space uses unseen rules. A “creature you can see” requirement is never met by position knowledge alone. Area effects can target legal points under their own rules.

currentGoverningExcerpts.heading: Gain a level
currentGoverningExcerpts.exactText:
## Gain a level

Opening campaigns officially use milestones. The Director’s announced milestones grant advancement; a CR-to-XP UI helper is not the official Opening reward law. The book’s cumulative XP thresholds remain available for tables using optional XP. See [XP provenance](XP_ADVANCEMENT_CANON.md).

Each earned advancement adds one total character level, to a combined maximum of 20. Choose one existing Base class to advance, or enter one new Base class if eligible. Process multiple earned levels one at a time; do not skip intervening choices.

1. Record the gained class and new class level. Recalculate total level and PB: +2 at total 1–4, +3 at 5–8, +4 at 9–12, +5 at 13–16, +6 at 17–20.
2. Add one new unspent Hit Die of the gained class’s size. Previously spent Hit Dice remain spent; gaining this die does not refresh any earlier die. For HP, roll that die or use its fixed rounded-up average: d6→4, d8→5, d10→6, d12→7. Record the base result before CON. This includes taking a new class’s first level after character level 1; maximum first-level HP is never granted again.
3. Apply exactly the gained class’s acquisition row, automatic improvements and class-level prerequisites. Complete its choices and any newly reached Arch/Hero gate. Automatic grants, scheduled selections and ASIs are distinct; do not pay a selection twice or grant an extra selection because the same feature appears in a legacy table.
4. At an ASI milestone, increase one score by 2 or two scores by 1, normally no higher than 20, or select one eligible operational feat. Ordinary milestones are class levels 4/8/12/16/19; Oracle uses 4/8/14/19. Follow any already-reviewed specific exception. No starting feat or repeatable feat is implied. [Eight complete feat options](FEAT_PLAYTEST_INDEX.md) do not make the other 327 complete.
5. Update legal repertoire, prepared capacity, class scaling and resource maxima at the gained **class** level. Use class-specific Druid preparation, Wizard spellbook/matrices and other explicit rules before generic acquisition defaults. New capacity does not provide an unnamed spell, an unearned choice, a filled Echo record or an extra prepared spell without the required preparation procedure.
6. Recompute base maximum HP from all attained-level records using current CON: sum(max(1, each stored base value + current CON modifier)). Then apply the separate [maximum-HP ledger](MAXIMUM_HP_PLAYTEST.md), including compatible bonuses, reductions and systemic factors. Do not feed an already modified maximum back in as the base.
7. Keep current HP and spent resources unchanged except for a downward clamp when a maximum falls. An ordinary level-up is not healing or a rest: it cannot revive a downed/dead character, erase Wounds or refill already spent Hit Dice, RP, RC, class pools, item charges or uses. Newly granted features still follow an explicit acquisition/initialization clause if they have one; “gain a maximum” alone does not mean “restore current.”

**New HP completion:** each level’s HP contribution has a minimum of 1. Recompute those individual floors after permanent CON changes. This preserves retroactive CON adjustment without a naive level×modifier-change formula that can bypass a floor. Capacity increases grant no current HP; decreases can clamp current HP without damage/healing triggers, consistent with the reviewed maximum-HP interface. Temporary ability effects follow their own actual source rules rather than being silently treated as permanent advancement.

No banked card selections, free retraining or free respec is introduced. Use an existing explicit replacement/retraining procedure where one exists.

currentGoverningExcerpts.heading: One shared RP pool
currentGoverningExcerpts.exactText:
## One shared RP pool

Calculate each eligible class’s own current candidate RP pool at its own class level. Sort these classes by:

1. Caster tier: Full (Cleric, Druid, Mage, Wizard), then Half (Paladin, Ranger), then Hybrid (Bard, Shaman, Mirrorsage, Crimson Agent), then Minor (Dragoon, Monk, Thief, Tinker).
2. Within a tier, higher class level first.
3. If class levels tie, higher actual RP pool first.
4. If both tie, the class acquired earlier first. Record that order; do not choose a different primary per cast.

Oracle, Soldier and Warrior contribute no RP pool. Maximum RP = the first class’s full pool + ceil(one quarter of the second class’s pool). With only one eligible class use its pool; with none, maximum RP is 0. Third and later eligible classes contribute no extra capacity, while retaining their earned class features and legal repertoire. Use current Core V2 candidate pools, not the older smaller companion-derived tables.

All RP-paid spells and techniques use this one merged pool unless an exact rule names another resource. RC, BG, Momentum, Ki, Conviction, Lay on Hands and other class resources remain separate. A change in the primary class or maximum is not recovery: preserve current RP and clamp only if above the new maximum. This can reduce maximum RP when a newly entered higher-tier class becomes primary; do not silently choose a larger lower-tier pool instead.

Each ordinary cast declares its casting class before costs. That class must independently know/prepare the spell, meet its school/rank gate and supply its own casting ability. Another class’s levels or repertoire cannot fill those requirements. Where two classes know the same spell, choosing its casting class does not create a second spell identity.

currentGoverningExcerpts.heading: Shared strain, recovery and concentration
currentGoverningExcerpts.exactText:
## Shared strain, recovery and concentration

Keep one character-wide Dissonance number and one Refrain history across classes. For a cast, evaluate limit = max(4, 2 + total-character PB + max(0, the actual casting-class modifier)). Apply the existing surcharges, ranked-cast cutoff, repetition and explicit class exceptions from [shared class rules](CLASS_PLAYTEST_RULES.md). Switching casting class does not clear either history; the same spell identity still repeats. Class cadence benefits require their actual ownership and trigger conditions. Idle decay and Grounding occur once per character turn, not once per class.

Generic Retune happens once per eligible completed short rest for the character. It restores max(0, round-half-up(maximum RP / 4) + the current primary RP class’s casting modifier), capped at the merged maximum, and clears Dissonance. Optional once/day meditation uses that same primary class’s positive modifier and the existing PB-based strain reduction. Long-rest RP recovery restores the merged pool under the existing recovery rules. None of these generic procedures duplicates because the character has more classes or recovers a different named resource without its own rule.

Oracle Revelations use RC and do not generate ordinary Weave strain unless expressly stated; they do not clear existing strain/Refrain from another class. One ordinary concentration slot is shared across classes, with only the exact already-reviewed linked-effect exceptions such as Spell Tether, Tethered Cast and Crimson Harmony. No generic Overcast option is reintroduced.

currentGoverningExcerpts.heading: Select a spell
currentGoverningExcerpts.exactText:
## Select a spell

1. Choose the class through which you are learning/casting it. Check that class's school access and minimum **class** level on the card.
2. Use that class's spell rank and Core V2 cost. A different eligible class may receive the same spell at a different rank and level.
3. Record it in your allowed known, prepared or spellbook choices. An eligible catalog entry is not an automatic grant. Wizard and Druid keep their explicit preparation systems; fallback counts apply only where the class has no more specific rule.
4. Select only a spell marked `operational-playtest-draft` in this packet, or an operational spell expressly supplied by a class card. Other records stay visible in the unfinished queue.
5. A class card and an ordinary spell with the same name remain separate records with separate acquisition and costs. Knowing one does not grant the other. Oath spells, Matrix techniques and similar class spells use their own card.

Oracle uses RC and its Mystery/Curse system. Soldier and Warrior have no general Weave access. Dragoon first gains ordinary magic at class 3; Paladin at class 2. Sufficient RP, total character level, a class feature with the same name, or a borrowed spellbook cannot bypass a gate.

currentGoverningExcerpts.heading: Resolve a cast at the table
currentGoverningExcerpts.exactText:
## Resolve a cast at the table

1. Verify the available Action/Bonus Action/Reaction, its exact trigger, components, targets, range and line of effect. No legal target means no activation or payment. A target in an area still needs the card's eligibility. Total cover blocks direct targeting unless expressly overridden.
2. Choose a spell from your actual repertoire. Determine its class-specific rank and RP cost: rank 0–9 costs **0/2/3/5/7/10/13/17/21/26**. Add explicitly printed extra costs; Resonance Shield adds 1 RP even when the caster receives it as a cantrip. Generic Overcast is excluded.
3. Read Dissonance **before** casting. Limit = max(4, 2 + PB + max(0, casting modifier)). At limit/limit+3/limit+6, ranked spells cost +1/+2/+3 RP. At limit+6 ordinary rank-1+ casting is blocked. Cantrips have no strain surcharge but still build Refrain. An expressly granted traumatic-casting exception pays the cost and its printed trauma; it grants neither rank nor repertoire access.
4. Commit the legal cast's RP, materials and other printed costs before any attack/save or interruption. Perform its components and establish concentration if required, ending incompatible prior concentration. An ordinary missed, saved-against or countered legal cast refunds nothing and never restores displaced concentration.
5. At this cast's beginning, apply ordinary Dissonance and Refrain once: 0 base for rank 0, 1 for ranks 1–5, 2 for ranks 6–9; consecutive same-named casts add Refrain +1/+2/+3, capped at +3. First cast or a different name adds +0. Apply the class's exact protected reduction, routing or vent and any hook whose printed trigger is beginning/casting. Weapon or idle turns do not reset the previous name/Refrain unless the class expressly says so. This chronological commitment occurs before the Counterspell window; a later Reaction cast updates its own history, and resuming the earlier cast does not update that history again.
6. Open legal cast-interruption Reactions, resolving nested counters last-in, first-out. A surviving cast then resolves its effect: spell attacks are d20 + PB + the actual casting ability modifier; save DC is 8 + PB + that modifier. Use the exact card's hit/failure/success results and ordinary damage/conditions. Outcome-dependent class hooks occur only at their printed timing and with the required actual result. No automatic cantrip scaling applies. A negated spell grants no success/hit/damage effect merely because its casting cost was paid.
7. Record concentration, exact expiration, per-rest use, summon and companion command obligations. A second spell cannot supply an ungranted Action, duplicate concentration or resource reset. A readied spell commits this casting sequence at preparation; release has no second cast, cost, cadence update or Counterspell window.

Countering requires an actual operational spell or class card, its repertoire/access and a legal remaining Reaction. The ordinary Counterspell is now reviewed; it is separate from the Mage and Wizard class cards. Dispel Minor, Dispel Resonance, Dispel Magic (Lesser) and Dispel Magic use their exact individual scopes. Rank-limited dispels inspect the original generating cast's spell rank, not RP cost or the dispeller's rank. Higher and unassigned source variants retain their own unfinished status.

currentGoverningExcerpts.heading: Counterspell checks and interruption
currentGoverningExcerpts.exactText:
## Counterspell checks and interruption

The [exact notebook review](../../../../docs/audit/2026-10-08/full-game/GPT_ABJURATION_RANK2_3_EXACT_REVIEW.md) confirms this authored timing interface and corrects the earlier binary-check proposal using the existing [Core roll rules](CORE_RESOLUTION_PLAYTEST.md). This is a tabletop procedure; the pricing helper does not implement nested reactions.

Ordinary Counterspell uses its casting class's actual spellcasting ability + PB against **DC 10 + twice the triggering spell's actual rank**. The class Wizard/Mage cards retain their printed Intelligence + PB check and their own acquisition, cost, rank and recharge. Apply the existing fixed-DC task degrees and natural shifts, then collapse Critical Success/Success to success and Failure/Critical Failure to failure. No extra critical counter effect is invented. It is neither a spell attack nor a saving throw.

| Natural d20 + modifier | DC | Existing task result | Counter result |
|---|---:|---|---|
| 20 + 0 | 22 | Failure improves to Success | Success |
| 1 + 9 | 10 | Success worsens to Failure | Failure |
| 1 + 20 | 10 | Critical Success worsens to Success | Success |

The target must be an actual pending spell with a recorded rank. The Director may use hidden source data without revealing the spell's identity/rank; attempting grants no free identification. An unassigned rank is not automatically zero. A source-defined technique is not counterable merely because it spends RP or resembles magic.

A creature normally attempts Counterspell once against a particular pending cast, across its ordinary and same-named class sources. Another Reaction alone does not supply another attempt. An exact source expressly granting an additional attempt against that same cast overrides the default. After failure, another eligible creature may react; after negation there is no further trigger. Counterspell is itself a spell and can be countered. Resolve nested counters last-in, first-out and resume surviving parents without recasting, paying again, or replaying their earlier Refrain/Dissonance. Negation refunds no costs and restores no prior concentration. Countering one spell is not whole-Action/turn hard denial and does not spend that combined ledger.

currentGoverningExcerpts.heading: Components, summons and ongoing effects
currentGoverningExcerpts.exactText:
## Components, summons and ongoing effects

**V** requires audible speech; **S** requires a free hand or a class feature expressly permitting the gesture; **F** is the class's ordinary casting focus. Core's M/F shorthand is interpreted here as the existing focus alternative. No unspecified costly or consumed material is added. These hand/focus conventions are provisional and may require equipment integration. A spell with V is blocked by an effect explicitly preventing verbal casting.

Summon stat blocks use their printed AC/HP/attack die. Where absent, saves use the owner's PB, other ability checks use +0, walking Speed is 30 feet, and there are no unstated creature immunities or extraordinary senses. Unless a card explicitly gives another bounded range, a commanded companion must be within 60 feet and able to perceive its owner. All one owner's companions share one Bonus Action command and **one damaging action total per round**. Without a command they move and Dodge. A replacement requires the full casting cost. No summon grants loot, a reusable corpse or resource-generating death trigger.

The [rank-2 Conjuration review](../../../../docs/audit/2026-10-08/full-game/GPT_CONJURATION_RANK2_EXACT_REVIEW.md) approves this specific companion overlay: **when an exact companion source prints multiple attacks as one damaging action, those attacks are components of one commanded offensive action and consume the owner's single offensive-companion allowance unless that source expressly grants otherwise.** Summon Air Pet explicitly makes its two source attacks within that one action; no second command/action or remaining offense for another companion is created. Its fixed AC15/HP20/two 1d6 attacks do not inherit generic companion scaling.

Planar Ally (Minor) uses a finite NEW summon-only profile for the source's intended CR-1 role. The bounded public bestiary scan did not establish an eligible published exact-CR1 extraplanar creature; this card does not certify its CR or rewrite a bestiary entry. Summon Weaponry Satchel has finite conjured contents tied to one duration, with a narrow exception only for an already resolving immediate use. Alignment Weapon's suppression default applies only to that printed card.

Resonance Well rolls one 1d4 total reserve. Its separately named creation and receipt uses commit before prevention and reset only through each character's beneficial long rest. These limits neither share nor reset Kindle or Mod Rod records. Read the exact cards and [rank-2 status](CONJURATION_RANK2_REVIEW_STATUS.json); pricing/schema checks do not execute these effects or certify balance.

The [rank-3 Conjuration review](../../../../docs/audit/2026-10-08/full-game/GPT_CONJURATION_RANK3_EXACT_REVIEW.md) adds seven bounded cards. Earth Pet's knockdown is Prone, not positional movement; generic push/pull immunity does not automatically prevent it. Burst of Flamewind affects every creature the caster ordinarily classifies as an enemy at a known location in its cone, with automatic source damage and a save controlling only its push.

Elemental Displacement selects a nearby willing recipient and a perceived destination; its teleport path is not constrained by intervening terrain. Spectral Steed actually crosses planes to a known site, once per steed attempt. Its 350-pound **and** 12-Load limits count the rider's body and all gear, including melded equipment. The reviewed correction from the conference's proposed6Load avoids excluding all gear from a Medium rider; ordinary Burdened applies at6Load. Read the exact mount/command/arrival procedure; it does not close general mounted combat.

Resonance Conduit transfers already-existing RP between two separate pools, with committed deductions, gated credit, and no resource creation or daily-ledger reset. Renewed consent cannot revive an ended application, but a new legal paid cast may create a new one. Faction Portal provides actual one-way travel to a known HQ on the same or another plane. Its positive-standing predicate uses the current canonical reputation record without migrating its scale. Travel may bypass a geographic route; elapsed clocks, cargo custody, contamination, claims, arrival law and settlement remain actual procedures. These cards do not declare automatic Extraction success or invent a blanket prohibition on planar escape. [Review status](CONJURATION_RANK3_REVIEW_STATUS.json) preserves the manuscript/runtime/balance distinction.

 Noncombat helpers cannot attack or operate combat items.

A cantrip that stabilizes restores no HP and removes no Wound. Mending cannot replace finite machine repair or refresh ammunition, charges, duration or class resources. Created tools, servants and water obey the explicit card limits; a spell does not silently pay wages, produce saleable materials or erase abstract expedition Supply.

All hard whole-Action/turn denial uses one combined **source-character/target/encounter** record across that character's spells, class features and companions. Once used, later hard-denial riders from that source fail; damage and soft riders resolve as printed. Boss immunities remain effective. Same-stat flat bonuses use the strongest; same-name dice bonuses do not stack. Apply one allowed bonus-die spell per roll in this packet unless a reviewed feature explicitly permits more. Temporary HP never add together. Copies never generate copies, class procs or resource loops.

currentGoverningExcerpts.heading: Mark Omen and Fate Coin: reviewed spell-specific rerolls
currentGoverningExcerpts.exactText:
## Mark Omen and Fate Coin: reviewed spell-specific rerolls

NEW scoped DE4-GUARD-01 amendment: Mark Omen, Fate Coin and Fate Reversal share one guard: an original roll event and its entire replacement lineage may receive at most one reroll from any of these three spells, across all casters, coins, marks, Fate Reversal permissions and recasts. Reserve this allowance at the first legal activation's commitment, not after the replacement die resolves. For a multi-die roll, the whole set/pool is one original roll event; the resulting attack's separate later damage roll is a different event. A shared area-damage roll remains one event even when applied to several creatures. Other exact class reroll features keep their own permissions and timing, but do not erase this guard or create a fresh lineage for these three spells. If competing declarations are simultaneous, use current initiative order; outside initiative use stable actor IDs then stable source/application IDs fixed before the original event, with the same stable tie-break for initiative ties. Only the first legal commitment spends its own actual mark, coin or Fate Reversal permission and any Reaction required by that source; a later declaration barred by this guard spends nothing. No new Action, roll event, cast, payment or duplicated outcome hook is created by replacing dice. This guard extension and the explicitly proposed DE4-RNG-05 digital mapping preserve each source's distinct replacement unit and eligibility. Mark Omen still replaces the caster's own marked-target attack d20 procedure with no additional Action or Reaction; Fate Coin still changes exactly one eligible engine RNG die component through its holder's actual Reaction and30-foot perceived-event interface; Fate Reversal still requires its own Reaction, pending permission, eligible complete attack/save/check d20 procedure and60-foot perceived-event interface. No class feature is added to this family merely because it changes a roll, and this amendment grants no new access to hidden dice or any source's otherwise ineligible roll. Apply DE4-RNG-05 in full; its player-information boundaries never grant hidden RNG access.

The [rank-1 Divination exact review](../../../../docs/audit/2026-10-08/full-game/GPT_DIVINATION_RANK1_EXACT_REVIEW.md) established that Fate Coin waits until the **complete original roll event** is rolled and its faces are available under the information rules then specified. It then replaces only one chosen die before consequences apply. Mark Omen replaces the caster’s complete attack d20 procedure before hit/miss resolution. Neither creates another attack/cast, rerolls an established resource reserve, reverses applied consequences or duplicates costs/hooks. A Well’s initial reserve die may be changed before the reserve is established. These two spell grants do not rewrite the Oracle, Mirrorsage or other class reroll contracts. The NEW pending DE4 amendment separately proposes the three-spell guard, DE4-RNG-05 engine interpretation and DE4-PRESENTATION-06 source-specific disclosure policy. Those later proposals were not part of the earlier rank-1 review; they require their own exact acceptance.

The same review preserves actual distant hearing, concealed-entrance revelation, creature sight through non-solid obscurity, willing memory-sharing, and actual faction/alignment/Corruption information. Warning Ward uses established hostility and an entry-triggered six-elapsed-second glow; it does not infer hostility from creature type or faction. Alignment Sense retains its source-defined rank-1 redundancy as an open balance question. [Review status](DIVINATION_RANK1_REVIEW_STATUS.json) records manuscript scope; no full information/roll-system runtime or human balance is certified.




NEW DE4-RNG-05 proposal under the owner's video-game-only directive. Authored dice are engine RNG operations, not physical tabletop objects. The actual conjured Fate Coin remains its existing physical game-world item with the same body, custody, hand, HP, duration and consumption. A roll event has an immutable original-event ID, replacement-lineage ID, actual generating entity/local event, original source, stable ordered component IDs, original modifiers/advantage state, target set and source-defined visibility grants. Finish the complete original RNG operation before any of these reroll permissions can commit; commit before its consequences. Fate Coin selects exactly one component of the complete eligible original operation and draws the same die type once; recompute its original reduction/selection with every other component unchanged. Mark Omen and Fate Reversal replace their own complete eligible d20 procedure. These distinctions survive digital implementation.

An engine's knowledge, logging, debug access, animation, a player's camera, knowledge of the seed, or prediction of a hidden outcome grants no character/player permission. The entire original die-result set must already be available to the acting player under the original event's established gameplay-information policy, and the source's actual perception, range, line-of-effect and resource predicates must independently pass. No eligible prompt, selectable event identifier or failure reason may reveal an otherwise hidden event. If the original source has no established visibility grant, these spells grant none; a source-specific presentation decision must be authored separately. A visible summed total alone does not reveal otherwise hidden component faces or grant a one-component choice. A fixed or automatic result with no actual RNG operation supplies no reroll event. Source-defined finite uniform 1dN random draws are eligible for Fate Coin only when their original result set is already available and the other source predicates pass; an empty set creates no draw, and the previously snapshotted candidate set never changes on replacement. Arbitrary simulation RNG, generation seeds and unexposed loot/world generation are not made eligible merely by existing in engine memory. No additional replacement RNG is consumed for a rejected preflight or a paid-but-blocked alteration; record the committed cost and guard separately from whether a new draw occurred.

Serialize legal commitments through the actual gameplay event queue. Simultaneous candidates use current initiative order; ties use stable preexisting actor ID then stable source/application ID. Outside initiative use those stable actor/source IDs fixed before this original event was generated. Network arrival, frame rate, client/UI order, reopening a prompt and a new replacement ID cannot change priority or create a new original lineage.
