## Removing suppressed Bleed and fire

Cures examine present, unexpired, not-ended records, including temporary suppression/acquired immunity. Initial immunity that prevented application leaves nothing to cure. Damage arbitration and active hooks still exclude suppressed/immune records.

Medicine selects one present eligible Bleed before rolling its printed/source/fallbackDC. A legal positive-potential magical heal invokes every present applicable Bleed endpoint; each Blood Curse instead receives its printedCON save. An actualHP-gain prerequisite still controls a source that expressly requires it.

A legal extinguish Action/full immersion ends all present ordinary-extinguishable fires within its scope; protected/special prerequisite fires persist. A permitted per-record fire DEX ending save remains available while suppressed when a future tick remains; no extra save after the final consumed tick. Cured records never resume when suppression ends.

# Eight feats: complete candidate rules

**REVIEWED / reference-VALIDATED for these eight full feats. Provisional playtest overlay; human numerical balance pending.** These rules cover Chef, Inspiring Leader, Empowered Summoning, Field Medic, Blood Ritual, Necrotic Affinity, Lifeleech and the Soul Cage **feat**. They do not authorize the separate Soul Cage spell or complete the other327 feat entries. Numerical balance still needs human playtests.

The335 original feat objects are preserved. [Actual GPT closure](../../../../docs/audit/2026-10-08/full-game/GPT_BUFFER_FEAT_FINAL_CLOSURE.md) reviewed131 targeted checks and2,520 funding boundary cases. The remaining327 feats require separate full-clause review. Source capture: `docs/audit/2026-10-08/full-game/BUFFER_FEAT_COMPLETION_SOURCES.json` from the game root. Decisions: `GPT_BUFFER_FEAT_FIRST_REVIEW.md`, `GPT_BUFFER_FEAT_BOUNDARIES.md`, `GPT_BUFFER_FEAT_FINAL_BRIDGES.md` in that directory. Later decisions supersede conflicting portions of the first draft. Reference adapter: `tools/buffer_feat_playtest_rules.py`; validation: `tools/validate_buffer_feat_playtests.py`.

## Shared rules

All eight feats are nonrepeatable and require an actual legal feat selection from the character's class progression. There is no extra universal feat schedule. Use the frozen class rules and each class's actual ASI/feat milestones; Oracle and other bespoke schedules retain their exceptions. Check a prerequisite at acquisition. Temporary later loss of an ability-score prerequisite does not revoke the feat; no general retraining rule is created.

“Spellcasting ability” requires a source that actually grants spellcasting and identifies a legal casting ability. Having RP, Revelation Charges or another magical resource is insufficient. A source's statistics do not transfer ownership of another creature's attacks to the statistic provider.

An ally includes the user unless a rule says **other**. Targets must satisfy their source's range, perception, line of effect and creature/living/willing restrictions. A target is counted once through multiple representations. No feature creates a new Action, Bonus Action, Reaction, command or turn unless it says so.

Temporary HP use the world's single grant ledger. Keep only the strongest current grant; an equal offer retains the old grant. Pay legal costs before this comparison. Rejected offers do not refund resources or recipient entitlements. A default-lifetime grant ends at the recipient's next completed long rest, depletion, replacement or applicable dependency ending. Explicit durations replace that default where stated. Temporary HP do not restore normal HP, wake a dying creature, remove Wounds, stabilize it or resurrect it.

Each turn/round/rest/death/physical body/food item/source activation has a persistent canonical identity. Extra Actions are not new turns. A genuine extra turn can satisfy a once-per-turn rule but does not create a new numbered round. Outside initiative use the world's authoritative six-second round-equivalent windows; entering/leaving combat preserves phase and never refreshes an entitlement.

## Chef — General; no prerequisite

During an actual long-rest attempt, use cook's utensils and spend one uninterrupted hour cooking. This is permitted light activity only when the normal long-rest procedure permits that hour; the feat does not enlarge the allowance. Designate one batch of1..current PB intended servings at cooking start. Only one batch may be designated per rest attempt and only one can gain potency per successful completed rest.

On successful cooking completion, consume one real standard ration or meal-equivalent ingredient per intended serving. Create exactly that many physical prepared-food items, each with its own identity. Their food exists immediately, but they gain no feat potency before the rest actually succeeds. If the rest fails, the ingredients remain spent and the food remains ordinary. An incomplete cooking hour creates no special food.

At successful long-rest completion, first resolve old rest-expiring effects and advance the rest epoch. Then snapshot the Chef's current PB and empower up to `min(physically prepared servings still present, current PB)` items. Each grants `2 × PB at batch finalization` temporary HP. A PB increase cannot manufacture more ingredients or servings; a decrease leaves excess prepared items ordinary.

A creature with a legal serving must spend one uninterrupted minute eating it. Completing a legal offer consumes the serving and the recipient's **Chef-family entitlement for its current completed-long-rest epoch**, even if an equal/stronger existing grant wins. This limit is shared across every Chef. The Chef's own rest does not reset another recipient's entitlement.

Potency ends at the earlier of24 elapsed hours from successful batch creation or the Chef's next completed long rest after the creation rest. An already consumed/discarded item never returns. Expired potency leaves ordinary food, with no magical premium value. Potency expiration does not end a previously granted shield; that shield has the recipient's default lifetime.

Chef servings are distinct from crafted Feast recipes. Chef grants no recipe ingredients, crafting checks, RP restoration, creature traits or recipe power. It does not occupy the recipe system's one-feast-at-a-time slot. A lawful recipe rider can coexist with a Chef rider; temporary HP still do not stack. One physical meal cannot claim both effects unless an exact recipe expressly supports it. Recipe-specific ten-minute eating, longer crafting and materials remain independent.

**NEW:** the finite batch transaction, quantities, preparation/eating times, recipient-family cap, potency expiry and explicit no-duplication/economy bridges. The source's long-rest cooking role is preserved.

## Inspiring Leader — General; Charisma13+

Speak for ten uninterrupted minutes. At the start, select up to your current PB **other** willing creatures within30ft. Snapshot your character level and actual signed Charisma modifier then. Each selected creature must remain in range, hear and understand you throughout. No replacements or retargeting during the speech.

On completion, each continuously eligible recipient receives `max(1, snapshotted level + actual CHA modifier)` temporary HP with default lifetime. Each recipient can receive one legal Inspiring-Leader-family offer per its own completed-long-rest epoch, shared across all speakers. An offer rejected by stronger/equal temporary HP still consumes the entitlement.

If one listener loses eligibility, only that listener misses the benefit. If the speaker becomes Incapacitated, cannot continue speaking or abandons the speech, the whole unfinished performance fails. Interrupted speeches spend no recipient entitlements and have no owner per-rest use; the speaker may begin again. Later changes in the speaker's statistics do not change this performance's snapshot. Temporary CHA below13 after acquisition does not disable ownership.

**NEW:** other-creature restriction, count, range/language/presence gates, amount, snapshots and family rest limit.

## Empowered Summoning — Magic; Charisma14+

When your actual source activation genuinely creates a new finite summoned creature, offer it `2 × your PB at creation` temporary HP. Its lifetime is default recipient long rest, also ending when that creature instance ends. Returned/revived preexisting bodies, persistent companion redeploy/rebuild, Mage bound returns, Ranger bonds and devices do not qualify merely by appearing again.

Record a lineage key containing the owner, actual source activation root and creation-slot/body-lineage. Several distinct bodies created by one source each receive their own grant. Reissuing/recreating the same lineage never refreshes its creation grant or its round damage entitlement. A genuinely new activation paid/used under its own rules can create a new root. An Action, limited use, ritual use or item charge can be a real source cost; RP is not mandatory.

Each qualifying creature adds its owner's **current PB** to its first actual damage roll in each canonical round/window. Add this flat bonus once to a shared area roll, not once per affected target. A roll on an ongoing damage tick can qualify; fixed damage without a roll does not consume or receive the rider. Later rolls in that window gain nothing. A critical hit does not double this flat PB bonus.

The creature remains attacker and damage owner. This is not the owner's spell damage. All existing companion command, Bonus Action and offensive budgets remain unchanged. The feat grants neither an initiative entry nor an independent command budget.

**NEW integration:** exact lineage identity, recreation guard and preserved round phase. Creation amount and damage rider are tied to their exact respective PB timings.

## Field Medic — General; trained in Medicine

As a Bonus Action, use one actual healer's-kit use on one legally reachable living dying creature. Resolve the canonical automatic kit stabilization, including its normal1d4-hour recovery deadline. Inventory must contain a real remaining use; this feat invents no kit capacity. This is distinct from the ordinary Action/DC10 Wisdom(Medicine) stabilization option.

Whenever you actually cause a dying→Stable transition by **any legal method**, offer the target your PB temporary HP with default lifetime. Record the transition when it occurs. Already-Stable creatures cannot be stabilized again for a new grant. Record one entitlement per target + actual dying episode + feat owner, plus the actual stabilization event ID. Different owners do not share an artificial family lock, but each must actually cause a valid transition. A new episode requires a genuine exit from the old dying episode and later entry into dying; damage absorbed entirely by temporary HP does not create one.

If you also possess Battlefield Medic's separately sourced Trauma Response, first record the actual kit stabilization, then resolve that background's independent1HP recovery, then resolve Field Medic's temporary-HP offer. The later1HP does not erase the stabilization trigger. The feat itself provides no normal HP, consciousness, Wound removal or resurrection. No background is granted by acquiring this feat.

**NEW integration:** event/episode anti-replay identity and ordering with independent recovery; the broad “when you stabilize” trigger is preserved.

## Blood Ritual — Magic; Constitution13+ and character level4+

Perform a ten-minute ritual once per completed long rest. Commit the use at ritual start. Snapshot your character level, PB and selected targets then: yourself plus up to PB **other** willing allies. Each ally must remain within10ft throughout, witness the ritual and voluntarily contribute a drop of blood. There is no normal-HP payment. No substitutions are allowed after starting.

At completion, offer yourself `2 × snapshotted character level` temporary HP with default lifetime. Each continuously eligible selected ally receives `snapshotted character level` temporary HP for one elapsed hour. A departed/ineligible ally loses only its own benefit. Your interruption fails the whole unfinished ritual and the use remains spent until a real rest resets it.

You also gain advantage on your next actual saving throw against an effect explicitly classified as a curse or disease. This rider is independent of the shield: rejection, replacement or depletion of temporary HP does not remove it. It ends when you roll that qualifying save or complete your next long rest, whichever is first. Consume it on the roll even if advantage cancels disadvantage or the save fails. It neither cures nor waives Oracle's intrinsic Curse and grants no oath or transformation.

If completion is strictly before a long-rest endpoint, the self shield/rider expire at that rest normally. At an exact tied completion, resolve old rest expirations, advance the epoch/reset resources, finalize Chef if applicable, then complete the tied ritual; its new shield/rider belong to the new epoch. Its already-committed start use is never retroactively refunded.

**NEW:** PB ally cap, presence/willingness details, use timing and independent save-rider deadline. Self/ally amounts and the ally's hour follow the reconciled source.

## Necrotic Affinity — Magic; Religion proficiency **or** character level8+

You have resistance to necrotic damage. Once per actual turn, when you hit with a melee attack, you may add1d6 necrotic damage. Natural/form melee attacks and off-turn Reaction attacks can qualify. A critical hit doubles this die to2d6; extra Actions in the same turn do not refresh it, while a genuinely different extra turn has its own entitlement. The die is feat damage, not spell damage.

Preserve the previously reviewed absorption procedure: when a legal necrotic spell/supernatural packet reaches the post-passive-defense stage, you may pay your Reaction to prevent `floor(post-defense necrotic damage /2)` before the old temporary-HP buffer. Resolve the remaining canonical damage once. Afterwards, if the holder remains living, offer temporary HP equal to the prevented amount until the end of the holder's next original regular turn, using its real endpoint marker. A1-point packet spends the Reaction but prevents/grants0. New temporary HP cannot absorb that same packet. Use `BufferLedger.necrotic_affinity` and `finish_necrotic_affinity`; do not apply resistance or damage twice.

When a creature actually dies from a canonical fatal damage/death root containing positive qualifying necrotic harm **owned by you**, attach a Necrotic Affinity seal to that death instance for24 elapsed hours. This includes your spells, the feat die, Agony Lance or another genuinely personal necrotic source. It is not limited to the feat's1d6. Supplying a summoned/transformed creature's statistics does not make its damage yours.

A mixed-type fatal root qualifies if your positive resolved necrotic component belongs to that root and the root actually causes death; no counterfactual subtraction test. Direct Instant Death, fatal death failures at0HP, or a later consequence expressly preserving that necrotic causal root can qualify. Temporary-HP-only absorption with no harmful consequence does not establish a seal.

The seal blocks applicable resurrection with an **actual spellRank/effectiveRank0..5**. Never invent a rank for unranked class features. Reviewed Paladin Grace Reversal is rank5 and is blocked; ordinary Resurrection7 and True Resurrection9 are above this restriction. Other resurrection requirements and Soul Bind still apply independently.

Same owner/death instance does not duplicate; different owners can have separate endpoints, but boolean blocking does not compound. A seal ends by elapsed expiry or an exact source able to remove that blocker, not generic cure. A legal return to life closes that death instance; its historical seals do not persist onto a later death. Transformations never create a new soul/body identity to evade a seal.

**NEW integration:** actual-turn identity, rank translation and fatal-root/death-instance bookkeeping. The broader printed necrotic-kill scope is preserved, correcting the narrower first draft.

## Lifeleech — Magic; actual spellcasting ability

Before your spell's damage resolves, designate one eligible hostile target for that spell root and canonical round/window. Your first positive actual necrotic damage to that target in the window commits the entitlement, even if the eventual healing is0, prohibited, capped or unfunded. No retargeting after observing results; area spells do not harvest a separate heal from every target. The same continuing spell can qualify again in a later real round/window.

Raw self-healing is `floor(actual necrotic damage dealt /2)`. Use only the actual necrotic component, including actual temporary-HP absorption and normal HP lost under the existing actual-damage interface; no overkill. Targets must be genuine hostile opposition, not friendly/staged/trivial sacrifices or owner/ally-generated farming bodies. Natural attacks, Agony Lance and the Necrotic Affinity die alone are not spells. The feat removes no Wounds and cannot resurrect its dead owner.

**NEW finite resource — Lifeleech Recovery Reserve:** newly acquiring the feat starts at0. At each actual completed long rest set its capacity and remaining points to `2 × current character level`, snapshotted then. Level/PB changes between rests do not refill/recompute it. This reserve is neither RP nor Mutation Recovery Reserve. Persistent save imports must preserve validated spent state.

Run the ordinary two-pass healing modifiers/reductions/prohibitions. Preview uses available reserve to determine whether conditional bonuses requiring positive actual HP restoration qualify. Apply reductions before funding. Cap final legal healing potential by remaining reserve; spend that **entire funded amount** on commitment, including funded excess. All lawful healing bonuses consume this same reserve. Then restore HP subject to ordinary maximum HP and Critical ceiling, and calculate `genuine excess = max(0, funded amount − ordinary missing HP)`.

A broad HP-gain prohibition produces0 legal amount, spends0 reserve and creates0 excess. At reserve0 the round/root trigger still commits, but it produces neither restoration nor excess. Full HP can produce funded excess, but does not enable conditional bonuses requiring actual HP restoration. Critical's ceiling does not itself turn all unrestored points into excess.

Lifeleech provides no intrinsic excess converter. A separately authorized converter must have its own eligibility/cost/cadence/cap and consume each funded excess point once. An explicitly legal resource-output converter remains possible; incidental heal-triggered resource production is blocked. The child heal carries `noLifeleechRetrigger`, `blockHealCopyTriggers` and `blockResourceTriggers`; propagate these to downstream callers. The resource flag blocks incidental triggers, not an exact, separately paid excess-conversion transaction. No new resource converter is granted here.

Lifeleech also automatically collects one Soul Charge at an eligible hostile soul-bearing creature's actual death within30ft, perceived with legal line of effect. No crystal is required for Lifeleech's own collection. Use the shared resource/death rules below. Lifeleech alone cannot spend charges through abilities from the unowned Soul Cage feat.

## Soul Cage feat — Magic; level8+ and (Lifeleech **or** actual spellcasting ability)

On acquisition, lock one actually possessed spellcasting source/ability as this feat's DC provider. Agony uses that source's current normal spell-save DC. No freely switchable DC ability or general retraining is created.

**Shared Soul Charges:** each owner has one persistent pool0..3, shared with Lifeleech. A charge is a soul **spark/residue**, not custody of the whole soul. It neither prevents resurrection nor replaces/removes Soul Bind. The ordinary Soul Cage spell is a separate rank6/13RP spell awaiting its own operational review. Soulrender's separate whole-soul ritual unlock still requires actually binding the soul of a living named enemy; residue cannot satisfy it.

At an eligible hostile soul-bearing creature's actual death within30ft, with perception and legal line of effect, Soul Cage permits immediate optional capture with no Action or Reaction. A discrete physical black crystal must actually be possessed and available. Lifeleech collection is automatic and needs no crystal. Owning both never gives two charges for the same death.

Each owner permanently records the exact death event as evaluated, including ineligible events. There is no later corpse rescan after moving closer, gaining a feat/crystal or improving perception. For an eligible event, also reserve the immutable body for that owner's current completed-long-rest epoch. Declining or being at full capacity consumes that entitlement; there is no latent fourth charge. A new real death after resurrection is a new event, but the same body cannot supply the owner again in the same epoch. A future completed rest can permit a future new death, never the old corpse. Different owners evaluate independently.

Created/generated farming bodies and immutable object-origin transformed creatures are ineligible. Soul status otherwise follows actual source/canon or Director adjudication; this feat does not declare every undead/construct category soulless. Death/root/body identities persist through forms.

Charges live on the owner and do not decay automatically. Losing/destroying/transferring the crystal transfers or erases **zero** charges; Soul Cage capture/spending is unavailable without another actual legal black crystal. Another feat owner can use the transferred physical crystal for their own pool. There is no invented price, attunement, HP, durability or crystal charge capacity. During one uninterrupted quiet minute handling the crystal, you may voluntarily dissipate owned charges; this does nothing to any deceased soul.

**Shield:** Bonus Action; pay1 Soul Charge; one legal ally within30ft, including yourself; roll2d8 temporary HP with default lifetime. Pay before strongest-only comparison. An equal/stronger old shield does not refund the charge or Bonus Action.

**Agony Lance:** Action; pay2 Soul Charges; one perceived legal creature within60ft; CON save against the locked provider's current DC. Deal3d8 necrotic damage, half rounded down on success, then ordinary defenses/Core apply once. This is feat damage owned by you, not a spell, RP expenditure or spellcasting trigger.

The target also gains one **Agony healing-suppression family** record until the next committed ordinary HP-healing event with positive pre-reduction potential, or one elapsed minute. That next healing receives an exact×1/2 factor in the canonical healing pipeline. Save success or necrotic immunity affects damage but does not remove this separate rider. Multiple Agony Lances never multiply to1/4: a new paid application refreshes the single endpoint to `max(old expiry, new application+60s)` and retains contributor history.

Consume the suppression on the first applicable committed healing event even if a stronger arithmetic branch wins or actual healing is later capped/prohibited. Suppressed/inapplicable records do not apply or consume; absolute time continues. Temporary HP, stabilization, resurrection, prevention and maximum-HP changes are not ordinary HP healing and do not consume it. Removal requires an exact source capable of removing this magical suppression/debuff; generic cure is insufficient.

**NEW:** prerequisite parsing, residue identity, shared resource/death transaction, conduit role, activations/ranges/DC and the exact healing-suppression conversion. Original source IDs and relationships remain distinct.

## Reference integration and limits

`FeatWorld` takes the actual shared `BufferLedger` and `HealingCommitLedger`. Its rest wrapper processes the shared buffer epoch once; never also process that same rest separately through the buffer ledger. Host scheduler resolves deadlines before new events and supplies true completion timestamps, canonical round/turn IDs and continuous-eligibility records. Mere strings/certificates are not a permission to fabricate elapsed time, line of sight, a new body or a paid summon activation.

Host retains real inventory, geometry, conditions, passive resistance, attacks, saves, damage attribution, class acquisition and current life state. `kit_stabilize` returns the new canonical life state; then record any independent background healing before `finish_stabilization`. `finish_agony` emits one pre-defense damage instruction; caller resolves it once. `drain` returns already-resolved healing: publish its new state once, never heal again. Commit **all** ordinary healing through the shared commit ledger so Agony's one-shot record is consumed once.

Necrotic Affinity's established Reaction helper remains unchanged. General resurrection calls query seals using the exact active death instance and source rank while also checking their other independent soul/body restrictions. Form changes do not reset these histories. Soul Charge acquisition does not alter Soul Bind or whole-soul ownership.

These bounded functions and tests establish rule consistency. They are not a full world scheduler, inventory simulation, campaign economy, soul taxonomy, human balance certification or completion of the separate spell/prestige/recipe systems.

currentGoverningExcerpts.heading: One active shield
currentGoverningExcerpts.exactText:
## One active shield

Temporary HP is a single active grant with its own identity, source, owner, recipient, remaining points, endpoint and explicitly attached permissions. A larger new offer replaces it; a smaller or equal offer is discarded. Equal values preserve the existing grant and its deadline. Discarded shields do not remain underneath. A rejected offer cannot lend its duration or linked rider to the winner. A zero offer creates no grant.

Pay the legal source's printed costs before comparing shields. Costs are not refunded because the new shield loses. Druid Buffer Reserve pays the entire offered amount, not just the increase over an existing shield. Preflight actual source access, targets, geometry, actions, components and resources before paying anything; illegal activations spend nothing.

Unless the source states a different shield lifetime, a grant ends at the recipient's next completed long rest. “Until lost” or “until lost or replaced” only restates depletion; it does not exempt a grant from that default. Explicit fixed deadlines and source dependencies take precedence, even when they outlast a long rest. An ongoing ability's general duration does not automatically shorten an instantaneous shield that it generates.

Temporary HP absorbs post-defense damage before normal HP. It is not healing: it cannot stabilize, revive, wake an Unconscious creature, remove Wounds, reset death counters or pay direct/sacrificial HP costs. A living creature at0 can receive it without gaining any of those benefits. A dead body is not a valid holder. A prohibition on HP healing does not implicitly prohibit a separately legal shield.

currentGoverningExcerpts.heading: Exact endpoints and riders
currentGoverningExcerpts.exactText:
## Exact endpoints and riders

Use actual owner/recipient regular-turn markers, absolute deadlines and encounter identities, not extra-turn or copied clocks. Source-specific rules remain in the exact card; this table resolves the important ambiguities.

| Source | Shield endpoint / linked boundary |
|---|---|
| Crimson Bloodshield | End of its three owner turns. Its one Reaction is attached only to its accepted grant; depletion/replacement/expiry removes permission. |
| Bloodbond; Lingering Malice | Each trigger/pulse makes a default long-rest grant; ending concentration does not erase it. |
| Nature's Blessing; Dread Shelter; Nano-Aegis command | Start/cast/command shield uses default long-rest lifetime; Speed, DR and support mode keep their separate clocks. |
| Protective Programming | Offer before the triggering hit. Resolve that hit, then remove any remainder of this particular grant. A stronger unrelated shield that won comparison is unaffected. |
| Monk Support; Warder Arrow and capstone | Default long-rest grants. Permanent availability or an instantaneous attack is not a permanent shield. |
| Harmonized Core; Arcane Leech; Primordial Surge; King's Smite; Noble Bearing | Default long-rest lifetime, including the sources that merely say “until lost.” |
| Linked Ward | After the actual triggering packet, default long-rest grant. |
| Final Stand | After actual triggering packet; shield and triggered resistance end at the ally's next regular end. The redirection itself ends at the Paladin's next regular start. **New grammatical integration.** |
| Unbroken Covenant | Until the Lock ends; this clause is explicit in preserved source provenance. |
| Last King's Gift | After damage, until encounter end. Its existing death-prevention gate remains separate. |
| Soldier Rally Point | Shield until encounter end; next-save bonus only until Soldier's next regular start. |
| Soldier Rallying Cry | Encounter end. |
| Dragoon Bastion Descent | Shield until Dragoon's next regular start; resistance until used or that start; cleanse instantaneous. **New grammatical integration.** |
| Bear / Earth Warden | Bound to that form instance; no refill at renewal. |
| Mooncursed ally Howl | Independent default long-rest grants, surviving Druid reversion. **New bridge clarification.** |
| Overflowing Light | Original two-round endpoint; if this exact grant is still active with at least1 point, allow ending one actual Frightened, Poisoned or Staggered condition. Rejection, replacement, depletion or holder/dependency removal gives no cleanse. Mastery raises only the cap10→20. |
| Protective Verse | One-minute shield and a separate one-minute next-qualifying-save rider. The rider can survive shield replacement. |
| Arcane Sanctuary | Each accepted pulse until owner's next regular start or source end, whichever first. Its attack bonus is a separate zone effect. |
| Empowered Link | Half the eligible source numeric benefit, rounded down/minimum1 where applicable; shared benefit duration capped at owner's next regular end. It cannot share resources, Actions, resistance or other excluded effects. |

Other explicit minute, round, turn and encounter endpoints retain their exact source wording. Cleric return shields, Crimson Pact, Mirrorsage Ward profiles, Mage Resonance Shield and Soulbound use their printed one-minute deadlines. Light Binding ends at owner's next regular end. Momentum Shield, Bolstering Presence, Aura Surge, Black Manifestation, Final Command, Mutation Surge and Wizard Abjuration use their printed next regular start. Momentum Barrier lasts one minute. A source with no specified shield endpoint uses the default.

King's Smite and Noble Bearing first resolve their shared internal component: when Noble applies, produce one Noble offer instead of a King's Smite offer. Each is half actual radiant Smite damage, rounded down, capped atS+M. Then compare that one offer with the recipient's existing shield. Their word “replaces” does not override an unrelated equal shield. Transfer-generated shields use the prior redirection package's actual absorbed amount, single-root restrictions and source caps; they appear after the causal packet and cannot retroactively protect it.

Each excess-healing point has one conversion owner. A source that explicitly converts its own excess has priority over external generic converters. Channel Life's packet forbids excess-to-temp-HP conversion by any provider; independent fixed shields still resolve normally. These are the existing healing interfaces, not a second excess pool.

currentGoverningExcerpts.heading: Armor and shields
currentGoverningExcerpts.exactText:
## Armor and shields

Choose one applicable AC formula. Light armor adds the full DEX modifier to its printed base. Medium adds `min(DEX modifier, 2)`, including a negative modifier. Heavy uses its fixed AC without positive or negative DEX. Explicit separate AC bonuses apply only when their own requirements are met.

One usable equipped shield contributes its printed bonus: buckler +1, shield +2, tower shield +3. No second shield bonus. Elven weave's printed Stealth advantage uses ordinary advantage/disadvantage cancellation. Dwarven plate is AC 18; its descriptive superior protection adds nothing. Scale mail's description adds no slashing resistance. Tower shield adds no unprinted cover or additional movement penalty.

**Nonproficient worn armor.** Retain V6 disadvantage on STR/DEX ability checks, saving throws and attacks. Core replaces the older casting prohibition: spells remain permitted, but an RP-priced spell costs +1 RP once per cast and concentration checks/saves have disadvantage. Multiple nonproficient armor pieces never multiply this surcharge. A normal 0-RP spell using the RP price interface can cost 1 RP. Apply this ordinary price addition before the already reviewed eligible reductions and final Resonance Influence step.

**Nonproficient shield — new completion.** While using a shield without shield proficiency, apply the STR/DEX check/save/attack disadvantage. A shield alone adds neither Core's armor RP surcharge nor concentration disadvantage and does not prohibit casting. Core names worn armor for those casting penalties.

A charge-only ancestry spell, Oracle effect or other cast with no RP-price interface acquires no RP price or pool from nonproficient armor. Actual concentration still has disadvantage from nonproficient worn armor. Hands, spell components and other independent casting restrictions remain.

**Strength minimum — new completion.** If one or more equipped armor/shield records have a listed STR minimum you do not meet, reduce Speed by 10 feet total, minimum 0. This is not a minimum to equip; multiple deficient pieces do not stack the reduction. This penalty can coexist with Load/Burden.

The Dwarf's printed rule that Speed is not reduced by wearing heavy armor prevents this penalty when the deficient item is heavy armor. It does not waive Load/Burden, another movement penalty or a tower shield's separate STR minimum. If a table chooses V6's preserved optional encumbrance alternate, that alternate ignores the Armor Table Strength column; the active reviewed Load procedure is not that alternate.

| Equipment | Don | Doff |
|---|---|---|
| Light armor | 1 minute | 1 minute |
| Medium armor | 5 minutes | 1 minute |
| Heavy armor | 10 minutes | 5 minutes |
| Any shield | 1 Action | 1 Action |

One actual assisting creature halves doff time only; a shield still takes at least one Action. Additional helpers do not repeatedly halve it.

currentGoverningExcerpts.heading: Hands and focuses
currentGoverningExcerpts.exactText:
## Hands and focuses

A buckler straps to one forearm. Its partially available hand can carry a small nonweapon object, but supplies no free S hand, loading hand, second-weapon attack, two-handed weapon support or active focus manipulation. An ordinary shield or tower shield occupies one hand. Soldier Shield Trained is a specific selected-feature exception for its repeating-crossbow/strapped-shield use, with that feature's actual reload requirements.

A two-handed weapon requires both hands when attacking with it. Releasing one grip costs no Action; regripping is part of its next legal use. This does not free a hand already occupied by another object, restraint or incompatible anatomy.

F requires an actual focus legal for the casting source. A hand holding only that focus may manipulate it and supply S for the same cast; the focus itself is not a conflicting object. A weapon, shield, second object, loading requirement or other hand restriction can make that hand unavailable. An item independently serving as both weapon and focus can use this rule only when an actual source authorizes that item as the caster's focus.

A holy symbol may supply F while held, visibly worn or borne on a shield where that casting source permits holy symbols. A worn or shield-borne symbol does not supply a free S hand. V still requires actual audible speech, and neither a focus nor component pouch waives explicitly priced or consumed materials. The component pouch supplies its ordinary storage function; this guide does not give it a new universal F substitution.

The following focus assignments are **new class integration** for actual legal class spells requiring F. They grant no spells or resource pools. Exact class features may override their own focus rules.

| Casting class | Ordinary focus |
|---|---|
| Bard | One actual instrument |
| Cleric, Paladin | Holy symbol |
| Druid, Shaman, Ranger | Druidic focus |
| Mage, Wizard | Arcane focus |
| Mirrorsage | Steel mirror |
| Oracle | Divination token |
| Crimson Agent, Dragoon, Monk, Thief, Tinker | Token for that class |

Soldier and Warrior gain no spellcasting from focus ownership. An ancestry casting token remains ancestry-grant scoped and cannot substitute for a class focus. An explicitly granted ordinary background arcane focus or holy symbol retains its normal equipment function for a casting source already entitled to that focus category.

# Time Loop: reviewed foundational transaction kernel

**Status: REVIEWED / reference-VALIDATED within the bounded foundational scope. Full Time Loop remains unavailable.**

**Current-file qualification:** the original approval binds helper hash `b821829ed352e69ce1ecf3c3d753f0206c8f8d2ec5a5d64bc89d5fd7d8a72151`, preserved as `docs/audit/2026-10-08/full-game/temporal_playtest_rules_reviewed_foundation.py` at the game root. The current helper adds a control/pulse transaction adapter and regular-start phase tracking. Those extensions are now covered by the separate [bounded control/pulse review manifest](TEMPORAL_CONTROL_WORLD_REVIEW_STATUS.json), following actual notebook confirmation. They do not inherit the historical approval. The 76 foundation regressions still pass. See [integration progress](TEMPORAL_CONTROL_PLAYTEST.md).

This implements a bounded part of `oracle.supplement.spiral-touched.spiral-touched-boon-v`. It does not change the original source, enable the ability in the playable class catalog, or close the full temporal interface. The notebook's twelve decisions are the authority for this candidate: [boundary conference](../../../../docs/audit/2026-10-08/full-game/GPT_TEMPORAL_WORLD_BOUNDARIES.md).

## What is implemented

The reference restores an immutable initiative-start snapshot through a preflighted transaction. It handles a finite development scene containing canonical Core life states, action wallets, selected feat shields, a temporal healing-consumption ledger, explicit Soul Bind/death identities, physical provenance, finite level-ground geometry, reward opportunities, external dependency records and character memory. The existing shared `LifeState`, `Wallet` and `BufferLedger` objects retain their identities. Spent resources and historical event records remain current.

The restore is permitted only after a complete atomic combat event, before round four, with an available Reaction and an unspent actual long-rest use. It never interrupts a damage, healing or command transaction. Preflight checks all registered state, source policies, physical dependencies and placements before charging anything. A prepared plan becomes stale if the registered world changes before commit. The single-thread reference requires the host scene lock through preflight and commit. Each committed restore also retains an engine/Director audit frame with the previous and resulting field values; that audit is never a source of character memory. The existing canonical BufferLedger completed-rest epoch also governs Time Loop's own long-rest use; there is no independent rest counter to diverge.

At commit, encounter initiative and the snapshot's Action/Bonus Action/Reaction allowances, RC and declared per-encounter uses return. Every outstanding Oracle Time Loop Reaction debt overlays the restored budgets. Only the owner's actual normal regular-start refresh clears that owner's debt. The public `TemporalKernel.regular_start(actor, now)` obtains the actor's canonical Wallet internally; it accepts no Wallet argument and rejects actor aliases sharing one Wallet. The bounded scheduler enforces the next actor at the initiative cursor, allows one active regular turn, and advances the cursor/round only when that exact turn ends. An out-of-order or repeated start cannot refresh a Reaction or advance the actual regular marker. Genuine extra turns require the later source adapter and cannot be represented as regular starts. The new iteration has fresh round/turn identities; the rewind itself creates no turn start, pulse or recharge tick. Elapsed world time, real regular-marker count, RP and finite-use history remain unchanged.

## Conservation checks

| State | Bounded behavior |
| --- | --- |
| Core HP and Wounds | Restore numeric snapshot HP against the current legal maximum. A lower maximum clamps HP without damage or healing; a higher maximum does not increase snapshot HP. Critical Wound healing ceilings do not limit temporal assignment. |
| Maximum HP | Use the existing maximum-HP calculation and an exact source-ID temporal policy table. The three reviewed Monk trauma IDs may restore except after actual rest ending. Tough, Tough as Nails, Tenacity and Dark Fortitude use current permanent progression records; temporary endpoints on those passive records are rejected. Other sources, including valid ordinary max-HP sources whose temporal/lifecycle adapter is absent, reject this fixture. Current supported external records overlay the result. Structural progression changes reject without a dedicated adapter. The host supplies current legal base/stat values. |
| Stable recovery | Preserve its original world deadline and event identity. An already resolved or expired recovery cannot replay; this kernel rejects such restoration rather than inventing a recovery rule. |
| Temporary HP | Restore the same grant ID and original snapshot amount only while its source's deadline/rest epoch/entity dependency remains valid. Supported IDs are Chef, Inspiring Leader, Field Medic, Soul Cage, Empowered Summoning and Blood Ritual. Required canonical ledger fields, unique grant IDs, active target/state and positive remaining amount are validated. Unknown sources and linked riders reject the scene. |
| One-shot healing reduction | Keep canonical effect ID and all past events. Consumption keys include the iteration. Snapshot-available Agony can be available in a new iteration before its original expiry; snapshot-consumed or expired Agony remains unavailable. |
| Soul Bind | Original absolute deadline, exact death instance for bound-dead records. An active pending record requires a living, non-Stable, dying zero-HP target with no death-instance binding. Application and target identities must match. Undoing a later death removes that later active bind. No revival event or source cost is manufactured. |
| Rewards | A claim belongs to encounter origin, immutable reward source, opportunity kind and source-defined slot. Another death event or iteration cannot make another claim. |
| Physical derivatives | Traverse immutable provenance transitively. A wholly in-scope, reversible temporal entity can retire; its costs stay spent. Surviving harvested inventory, mixed material roots, external source slots or persistent enrollment conflicts block the restore. Already consumed material remains consumed. |
| Outsiders | Keep body state, inventory ownership, resource history and concentration records. A snapshot dependency must still exist exactly and refer to the same live concentration ID. New current dependencies targeting restored participants need a supported overlay; otherwise they block. Unimplemented external anatomy/control/suppression overlays also block. |
| Environment | Each anchor has an exact canonical physical identity. Restore snapshot environment existence together with its geometry; remove both the physical derivative and its geometry when retiring a later temporal entity. Plan all participant positions simultaneously. Reject overlap, loss of support, and restrictions to a protected outsider's previously reachable ground area. This is deliberately limited to a finite orthogonal level ground plane, not flying, elevation, portals or mandatory growth. |
| Memory | The invoking Oracle and their immutable snapshot allies retain only facts individually perceived, experienced or received. Retained memories accumulate across loops. Enemy player characters receive no special knowledge; no hidden roster or Director facts enter memory automatically. |

## What the agreed rules mean at the table

These examples explain the reviewed boundaries. They do not enable the full ability before its remaining integrations are complete.

| Situation | Result |
| --- | --- |
| At initiative, an ally has25HP. Later they fall to3HP and spend8RP. Time Loop succeeds. | They return to25HP, limited by their current legal maximum. The8RP remain spent. Their snapshot encounter allowances return where the source explicitly permits it. |
| The same ally's legal maximum has fallen to20 because a conserved source changed. | They return to20HP. The reduction is temporal normalization, not damage or healing, and creates neither Wounds nor resource triggers. A structural progression change without its adapter instead makes the restore unavailable. |
| An ally began with a6-point Soul Cage shield, later lost it, and the original grant remains valid. | The same shield returns with its snapshot6 points. The Soul Charge paid for it remains spent. This is not a new cast, grant or recipient offer. |
| Oracle A uses Time Loop. Before A's next actual regular turn, Oracle B uses it too. | Both Oracles retain their Reaction debts. Rewinding does not clear A's debt. Each debt clears only at that Oracle's genuine normal Reaction refresh. |
| A restored enemy dies again after its reward opportunity was already claimed. | That same reward cannot be claimed again. The source opportunity, rather than the new death event, determines whether it was paid. |
| A body part was harvested after initiative and still exists as somebody else's item. | The generic restore is unavailable: it cannot duplicate the body part or take away the current owner's item. A specifically reviewed reconciliation would be required. |
| An ally saw a hidden passage in the discarded timeline; another ally never learned about it. | The witness can retain that memory if eligible through the invoking Oracle's snapshot alliance. The other ally receives no automatic knowledge. The witness can tell them normally. |

An unavailable restore spends neither the Reaction nor the long-rest entitlement. The Director needs a complete, legal proposed state before resolving the ability; unresolved source interactions cannot be waived by calling a snapshot complete.

## Required integrations still missing

The minimum seventeen-domain review is not complete. Seven major integrations are unimplemented: actual concentration/transformation callbacks; Druid form and conserved recharge clocks; creature lifecycle/corpse/persistent assets; device lifecycle/stock/commands; remaining structures, Choir and control lifecycles; the complete FeatWorld; and source-qualified control/healing pulses. Even the implemented foundational domains are bounded by the input policies above. For example, the external concentration map is a dependency projection, not the callback-bearing live concentration adapter.

`TemporalKernel.support_report()` reports that limit. `playable_plan()` always rejects until the full implementation and independent review exist. `kernel_plan()` is a development fixture interface, not a replacement for the complete Oracle feature. The host must disclose every active integration. A supplied unsupported holder rejects preflight; an empty registration is not a certificate that a real game scene is complete.

`TemporalHealingCommitLedger` can be passed as the one canonical healing ledger to existing helpers. Its canonical return IDs preserve `FeatWorld.commit_healing` removal semantics, while its historical consumption tokens are iteration-qualified. Capture/preflight validate the live registry independently of `register()`: exact source/identity/absolute clock, canonical owner/target, boolean availability, and matching consumption-token/event history. External effect dictionary keys, effect identities, dependency identities and max-HP record identities must also agree. Agony creation/refresh/removal still needs the full feat adapter to synchronize active records; this kernel does not claim that synchronization exists.

## Validation and next review

Run `tools/validate_temporal_playtests.py`. The current suite contains 76 adversarial test methods. [Validation report](TEMPORAL_KERNEL_VALIDATION.json) records the tested helper hash. The initial 46-test packet, later 52-test packet, and [six independent findings](../../../../docs/audit/2026-10-08/full-game/GPT_TEMPORAL_KERNEL_FINDINGS.md) are preserved separately. The notebook [confirmed the original six repairs](../../../../docs/audit/2026-10-08/full-game/GPT_TEMPORAL_KERNEL_REPAIR_REVIEW.md), then identified three narrow identity/admission gaps. Those repairs and six additional test methods received [actual independent closure](../../../../docs/audit/2026-10-08/full-game/GPT_TEMPORAL_KERNEL_FOUNDATION_CLOSURE.md). The [review status](TEMPORAL_KERNEL_REVIEW_STATUS.json) binds that disposition to the exact helper hash; the originally submitted helper is preserved in the audit archive; the later extension has its own review manifest. Two invented maximum-HP source examples in the first review already fail the existing source constructor; the exact temporal table additionally rejects actual valid sources lacking a temporal policy.

Next, add the seven missing integrations and exact source policies, with their own independent reviews. Do not remove the Time Loop deferred status based on these tests. The final joint whole-game flow review and authorized GitHub push remain later gates.

The subsequent [control/pulse conference and first implementation bridges](TEMPORAL_CONTROL_PLAYTEST.md) have their own recorded scope: nine source-policy families discussed,22 payment/output checks and50 bounded live-holder transaction methods jointly reviewed. Full nine-family restoration remains unfinished, so the seven missing-integration count is unchanged.

The next [form/concentration parent policies](TEMPORAL_PARENT_PLAYTEST.md) are now source-discussed with the notebook, including all26 Druid profiles and explicit renewal/stabilization history. The [parent status](TEMPORAL_PARENT_REVIEW_STATUS.json) records ten cases and the corrected Action-budget wording. Runtime parent integration and its validation are still pending.

The [exact-parent reference transport extension](TEMPORAL_REFERENCE_TRANSACTION_REVIEW_STATUS.json) is now jointly reviewed:15 new checks plus the existing207 pass. The prior control-checkpoint foundation is preserved at `docs/audit/2026-10-08/full-game/temporal_playtest_rules_control_checkpoint.py`; the current kernel hash has its own explicit review manifest. Only identity transport/rollback is added. Active form admission and full parent restoration remain gated.

currentGoverningExcerpts.heading: Bleeding
currentGoverningExcerpts.exactText: ## Bleeding **Preserved Core text:** Take damage equal to proficiency bonus at the end of each turn. An action and Medicine check or magical healing ends it. **Effect:** At the end of the affected creature's regular turn, take damage equal to its current PB, unless the selected reviewed application prints a different magnitude. Use that application's specified physical type; if none, slashing. **Application:** Only explicit Bleeding applications create a source record. Record DC (or 10), magnitude, type and endpoint. **Duration and ending:** Persists until its source or applicable cure ends it. Self or adjacent helper spends an Action selecting one active eligible Bleed record before a WIS (Medicine) check: printed cure DC, otherwise recorded applying effect/class/spell DC, otherwise 10. Success or Critical Success ends that record only. One legal magical healing event with positive pre-cap/pre-prohibition potential ends all ordinary records with an automatic-healing endpoint, even at full HP or while Corrupted/Decay prevents actual HP gain. Each Shaman Blood Curse instead gets its own printed CON save. Explicit end-one/end-all removers retain exact scope and protected-source exceptions. **Stacking:** Independent source-owner records enter unified family arbitration at their actual marker. No DC tie-break or separate generic damage layer. Medicine ends one selected record; positive-potential magical healing ends all eligible automatic-cure records. **Immunities and specific exceptions:** Creatures explicitly immune to bleeding/blood-loss effects cannot gain it. Specific spell/class/item Bleeding numbers replace the generic PB magnitude only when printed. **Explicit integration decisions:** - NEW: affected-creature PB; explicit physical type or slashing fallback; source DC or 10; one regular-turn tick and strongest-record selection. - Source-faithful clarification: magical healing need not increase current HP to end Bleeding. - SUPERSESSION — NEW PROVISIONAL INTEGRATION: The unified Bleeding/ongoing-fire family registry supersedes earlier provisional clauses that selected generic records separately, used ending DC as a damage tie-breaker, cleared all generic Bleeding through one Medicine result, or used one Burning save to clear all generic Burning. Original Core quotations and raw review history remain unchanged. See CUSTOM_CONDITION_BINDINGS.md and the recorded GPT_GENERIC_CUSTOM_ALIGNMENT review. Provenance: Core V2 `books/player/Decennium_Descent_Core_Systems_Bible_v2_Known_Descent.docx`, zero-based all-XML heading paragraph 729, definition paragraph 730; both positions, exact text and book SHA-256 are verified against the approved book and retained in the [condition data](../../data/playtest/condition_playtests.json).

currentGoverningExcerpts.heading: Incapacitated
currentGoverningExcerpts.exactText: ## Incapacitated **Preserved Core text:** Cannot take actions or reactions. **Effect:** The creature cannot take an Action, Bonus Action or Reaction. Passive effects continue unless their own rules require consciousness or another condition disables them. Incapacitated by itself does not reduce Speed or prohibit speech. **Application:** Applied by a condition or effect that explicitly says the creature is Incapacitated. **Duration and ending:** Use the parent condition/effect's duration. **Stacking:** Does not stack. **Immunities and specific exceptions:** Current shared concentration rules end concentration immediately when the creature becomes Incapacitated. A specific effect may preserve a passive benefit through Incapacitation if explicitly stated. **Compatible V6/source details:** - V6 matches: cannot take actions or reactions. **Explicit integration decisions:** - NEW integration: Bonus Actions are included in unavailable actions. - Already explicit in CLASS_PLAYTEST_RULES.md: becoming Incapacitated ends concentration. Provenance: Core V2 `books/player/Decennium_Descent_Core_Systems_Bible_v2_Known_Descent.docx`, zero-based all-XML heading paragraph 749, definition paragraph 750; both positions, exact text and book SHA-256 are verified against the approved book and retained in the [condition data](../../data/playtest/condition_playtests.json).

currentGoverningExcerpts.heading: Restrained
currentGoverningExcerpts.exactText: ## Restrained **Preserved Core text:** Speed 0; attacks against have advantage, own attacks and Dexterity saves have disadvantage. **Effect:** Speed becomes 0 and cannot benefit from Speed bonuses. Attack rolls against the creature have advantage; its own attack rolls and Dexterity saving throws have disadvantage. **Application:** Only an effect explicitly inflicting Restrained applies it. **Duration and ending:** Use the applying effect's printed duration, save or escape rule. If an effect creates a physical restraint and provides no escape procedure, use the existing shared playtest escape procedure only if that source is eligible for it. **Stacking:** Multiple Restrained applications do not compound penalties, but all independently maintained sources must end before the creature is no longer Restrained. **Immunities and specific exceptions:** Restrained immunity blocks application. Teleportation does not automatically end a restraint unless it breaks the source relationship or the applying effect says so. **Compatible V6/source details:** - V6 adds that the creature cannot benefit from bonuses to Speed. **Remaining wider integration work:** - Final generic physical-restraint escape procedure in combat rules. currentGoverningExcerpts.heading: Silenced
currentGoverningExcerpts.exactText: ## Silenced **Preserved Core text:** Cannot use verbal components, command words, Chants, or audible coordination. **Effect:** The creature cannot use spell/ability verbal components, command words, Chants, or any feature requiring audible coordination. It may still think, perceive, move, use somatic/nonverbal abilities and use effects that explicitly function without sound. **Application:** Only effects explicitly inflicting Silenced apply it. **Duration and ending:** Use the applying effect's duration/end rule. **Stacking:** Does not stack. **Immunities and specific exceptions:** An ability explicitly usable without speech or audible sound is unaffected. Silence immunity blocks application only if explicitly defined. **Explicit integration decisions:** - Clarification: Silenced is not universal mental or magical shutdown. **Remaining wider integration work:** - Specific audible-command features must state whether they require being heard by recipients. Provenance: Core V2 `books/player/Decennium_Descent_Core_Systems_Bible_v2_Known_Descent.docx`, zero-based all-XML heading paragraph 769, definition paragraph 770; both positions, exact text and book SHA-256 are verified against the approved book and retained in the [condition data](../../data/playtest/condition_playtests.json).

currentGoverningExcerpts.heading: Exhausted
currentGoverningExcerpts.exactText: ## Exhausted **Preserved Core text:** Use the six-level exhaustion track; effects are cumulative and level 6 is death. **Effect:** Track 0–6 cumulative levels: 1 disadvantage ability checks; 2 half Speed after flat changes; 3 disadvantage attacks and saves; 4 maximum HP max(1,floor(otherwise-applicable maximum/2)); 5 Speed zero; 6 death. **Application:** An effect that grants one or more Exhaustion levels increases the track by that amount, maximum 6, unless it explicitly sets a level instead. **Duration and ending:** Eligible beneficial eight-hour long rest removes one level under CONDITION_RECOVERY_PLAYTEST.md, at most one generic removal per 24 hours. Source-specific prerequisites can block removal. Meeting a prerequisite such as Moisture Dependency immersion does not itself remove a level unless printed. **Stacking:** Levels add, maximum 6. Derive level-4 maximum from the otherwise-applicable current maximum, never a previously halved value. Clamp HP down when maximum decreases; raising maximum does not heal. Level-5 zero Speed overrides halving. **Immunities and specific exceptions:** An explicit Exhaustion immunity blocks levels. Removing Exhaustion from a dead level-6 creature does not restore life; resurrection is still required. **Compatible V6/source details:** - Level 1: disadvantage on ability checks. - Level 2: Speed halved. - Level 3: disadvantage on attack rolls and saving throws. - Level 4: hit point maximum halved. - Level 5: Speed reduced to 0. - Level 6: death. **Explicit integration decisions:** - NEW: maximum-HP floor 1, recomputation/clamping and flat-Speed-before-halving order. - NEW: finite generic long-rest recovery; source-specific removal blocks remain. - Recovered V6: six cumulative level effects. Provenance: Core V2 `books/player/Decennium_Descent_Core_Systems_Bible_v2_Known_Descent.docx`, zero-based all-XML heading paragraph 743, definition paragraph 744; both positions, exact text and book SHA-256 are verified against the approved book and retained in the [condition data](../../data/playtest/condition_playtests.json).
